commits.message:
[build](fix) Distinguish between local build and pipeline build wheel (#2798)

* Fix the wheel build issue

* Add a manual packet generation process

* Remove the redundant clone steps

* fetch npuir nested submodules single-level to avoid GitHub externals

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Wheel builds track the AscendNPU-IR stable branch, NOT the pinned submodule
+# gitlink (local developer builds use the pin): fetch the stable sources here
+# so the product build code just sees an existing tree and never reaches into
+# the CI workflow scripts itself. Needed both for the C++ plugin build
+# (add_subdirectory(third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR)) and for the
+# TRITON_BUILD_NPUIR=ON in-image fallback. Includes the nested third-party
+# submodules (llvm-project / torch-mlir / shmem). NPUIR_REF overrides the
+# branch with an exact SHA for the pinned-submodule verification wheel.
+#
+# Then freeze the gitlink for the rest of the image build: the root setup.py
+# (BackendInstaller.prepare) runs `git submodule update --init ascend` from
+# third_party, whose directory-prefix pathspec also matches the nested
+# AscendNPU-IR gitlink — with the pre-fetched tree at a different SHA (the
+# stable-tracking flows) that command would silently checkout the pinned
+# SHA back over it. submodule.<name>.update=none makes every in-image
+# `git submodule update` skip it; the product code's own guards never issue
+# a submodule command when the tree already exists, so nothing else changes.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+RUN NPUIR_REPO_BRANCH=${NPUIR_REF} bash .github/workflows/build/fetch-npuir-stable.sh third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR \
+ && git config submodule.third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR.update none
+
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Build the wheel with the target Python from the manylinux toolchain.
 # Put the pip-installed ninja/cmake ahead of the system ones on PATH.

           # Wheels are already zip-compressed; skip the re-compress pass.
           compression-level: 0
 
+  # Verification wheel for PRs that move the AscendNPU-IR submodule pin:
+  # builds "this PR's triton-ascend + the pinned npuir revision" — exactly the
+  # combination local users get — by compiling npuir in-image
+  # (TRITON_BUILD_NPUIR=ON) against the gitlink SHA passed via NPUIR_REF.
+  # The wheel is uploaded as a run artifact and linked from the job summary
+  # only; it is never published (nightly wheels keep tracking the stable
+  # branch). A full npuir compile takes hours, so the job runs only for pin
+  # changes — PRs triggered by the other paths exit early (green) — or on
+  # demand via workflow_dispatch with pinned_wheel=true.
+  Build-Pinned-Wheels:
+    name: Build pinned-submodule wheel (${{ matrix.config.arch }}-cp312)
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pinned_wheel)
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.runs_on }}
+    container:
+      image: swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/ascend-ci/cann:9.0.0-a3-ubuntu22.04-py3.12
+      # PYTHON under container.env: same ARC postStart-hook (buildkitd node
+      # pinning) requirement as Build-Wheels.
+      env:
+        PYTHON: cp312
+    # The in-image npuir compile is far slower than Build-Wheels' prebuilt-
+    # payload path, so allow more headroom than its 360 minutes.
+    timeout-minutes: 480
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        config:
+        - {runs_on: 'linux-amd64-cpu-4', arch: 'x86_64'}
+        - {runs_on: 'linux-aarch64-cpu-4', arch: 'aarch64'}
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v5
+
+      - name: Add git safe directory
+        run: git config --global --add safe.directory "*"
+
+      - name: Check for submodule pin change
+        id: pin
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -eu
+          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
+            # workflow_dispatch with pinned_wheel=true: always build.
+            echo "Manual dispatch; building pinned wheel."
+            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          # This workflow also triggers on other paths; only PRs that actually
+          # move the gitlink need the (expensive) pinned wheel. Shallow-fetch
+          # the recorded base commit and diff just the submodule path.
+          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
+          git fetch --depth=1 origin "${BASE_SHA}"
+          if git diff --quiet "${BASE_SHA}" HEAD -- third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR; then
+            echo "AscendNPU-IR pin unchanged by this PR; skipping pinned wheel."
+            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo "AscendNPU-IR pin changed; building pinned wheel."
+            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Resolve pinned AscendNPU-IR SHA
+        id: npuir-sha
+        if: steps.pin.outputs.build == 'true'
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -eu
+          PINNED_SHA=$(git ls-tree HEAD third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR | awk '{print $3}')
+          if ! printf '%s' "${PINNED_SHA}" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'; then
+            echo "::error::could not resolve the AscendNPU-IR gitlink SHA (got '${PINNED_SHA}')"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "Pinned AscendNPU-IR SHA: ${PINNED_SHA}"
+          echo "sha=${PINNED_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Build pinned wheel
+        if: steps.pin.outputs.build == 'true'
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
+        with:
+          context: .
+          file: .github/workflows/build/wheels.Dockerfile
+          build-args: |
+            MANYLINUX_IMAGE=swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/ascend-ci/manylinux:9.2.0-beta.2-a3-manylinux_2_34-py3.12
+            PYTHON_VERSION=cp312
+            # Full in-image npuir compile at the exact pinned revision: the
+            # Dockerfile pre-fetches NPUIR_REF (the gitlink SHA), build_npuir
+            # sees the existing tree, compiles it and bundles the payload.
+            TRITON_BUILD_NPUIR=ON
+            NPUIR_REF=${{ steps.npuir-sha.outputs.sha }}
+            TRITON_WHEEL_VERSION_SUFFIX=+pinned
+            BUILD_DATE=
+          cache-from: type=registry,ref=swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/modelfoundry/triton-wheel-buildcache:${{ matrix.config.arch }}
+          outputs: type=local,dest=./wheelhouse
+
+      - name: Upload pinned wheel
+        id: upload
+        if: steps.pin.outputs.build == 'true'
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          # Distinct from the nightly cibw-wheels-* artifacts: this wheel
+          # bundles the pinned-submodule npuir and is for PR verification only.
+          name: pinned-wheel-manylinux_2_34_${{ matrix.config.arch }}-cp312
+          path: ./wheelhouse/*.whl
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          compression-level: 0
+
+      - name: Write job summary
+        if: steps.pin.outputs.build == 'true'
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -eu
+          WHL=$(basename "$(ls wheelhouse/*.whl | head -1)")
+          {
+            echo "## Pinned-submodule verification wheel"
+            echo ""
+            echo "| | |"
+            echo "|---|---|"
+            echo "| Wheel | \`${WHL}\` |"
+            echo "| Arch / Python | ${{ matrix.config.arch }} / cp312 |"
+            echo "| triton-ascend | \`${GITHUB_SHA}\` |"
+            echo "| AscendNPU-IR (submodule pin) | [\`${{ steps.npuir-sha.outputs.sha }}\`](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/AscendNPU-IR/commit/${{ steps.npuir-sha.outputs.sha }}) |"
+            echo "| Download | [pinned-wheel-manylinux_2_34_${{ matrix.config.arch }}-cp312](${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-url }}) |"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
   # Installs the built wheels on real NPU pods and runs a representative
   # subset of the Ascend unit tests (vector add / softmax / matmul / layer
   # norm / attention / grouped gemm / argmax / cumsum / add / dot). This

@@ -0,0 +1,897 @@
+# Triton msdebug 使用指南
+
+## 简介
+
+MindStudio Debugger（msdebug）用于调试运行在昇腾 NPU 上的设备程序，支持源码断点、单步、变量与内存查看、寄存器读取、核切换、运行状态查询和异常算子 Core Dump 解析等功能。
+
+msdebug 适合排查以下问题：
+
+- Triton Kernel 运行结果错误；
+- `tl.load`、计算或 `tl.store` 阶段的数据不符合预期；
+- 多 Block、多核场景中，部分核的计算结果异常；
+- Kernel 运行卡住，需要确认停止位置；
+- NPU 发生 MTE、VEC、CUBE 等硬件异常；
+- 需要分析异常现场生成的 `.core` 文件；
+- 源码断点、行号映射或变量调试信息异常。
+
+msdebug 不用于调试 Triton 编译器 Pass 本身。如果程序在生成 `kernel.o` 之前已经编译失败，应使用 IR Dump、编译日志以及 GDB/LLDB 调试 `triton-opt` 或编译器进程。
+
+## 使用前准备
+
+### 环境准备
+
+- 请参考 [MindStudio Debugger 安装指南](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msdebug/blob/master/docs/zh/install_guide/msdebug_install_guide.md)安装 msdebug 工具。
+- 若要使能 msdebug 工具，需通过以下两种方法安装 NPU 驱动固件（CANN 8.1.RC1 之后的版本且驱动为 25.0.RC1 之后的版本，推荐使用方法一）。
+
+**方法一**：驱动安装时指定 `--full` 参数，然后再使用 root 用户执行 `echo 1 > /proc/debug_switch` 命令启用调试通道，msdebug 工具便可正常使用。
+
+```bash
+./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full
+```
+
+**方法二**：驱动安装时指定 `--debug` 参数，具体安装操作请参见《CANN 软件安装指南》中的“[安装 NPU 驱动固件](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/canncommercial/83RC1/softwareinst/instg/instg_0005.html?Mode=PmIns&InstallType=netconda&OS=openEuler&Software=cannToolKit)”章节。
+
+```bash
+./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --debug
+```
+
+### 为 Triton Kernel 生成调试信息
+
+当前 Triton-Ascend 启用 msdebug 功能需要开启以下环境变量：
+
+```bash
+export LLVM_EXTRACT_DI_LOCAL_VARIABLES=1
+export TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO=0
+```
+
+| 环境变量 | 用途 |
+|---|---|
+| `LLVM_EXTRACT_DI_LOCAL_VARIABLES=1` | 开启 Ascend 后端局部变量调试流程，并启用相关 Location、NOP 和行表处理 |
+| `TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO=0` | 开启源码行号调试信息；当前后端默认可能关闭该信息，因此需要显式设置 |
+
+当前实现中，Ascend 后端会据此向后端编译器传递 `--enable-debug-info=true` 和 `--enable-debug-variables=true`。
+
+### 约束
+
+- 调试通道权限较高，不建议在生产环境长期启用；
+- 同一 Device 建议只启动一个 msdebug 会话，并暂停其他算子任务；
+- 被调 Python 程序最好只调用一个目标 Triton Kernel；
+- 首次排查时建议关闭 Autotune，固定一组 `BLOCK_SIZE`、`num_warps` 等编译参数；
+- 在线 msdebug 和异常算子 Dump 使用同一调试通道时可能冲突，不应同时开启；
+- 部分优化会改变变量生命周期，即使开启变量调试信息，也不能保证每个源码变量始终可打印；
+- msdebug、CANN、驱动、固件、芯片和 Triton-Ascend 需要使用相互兼容的版本。
+
+官方环境和约束说明可参考 [msdebug 使用前准备](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindstudio/830/ODtools/Operatordevelopmenttools/atlasopdev_16_0063.html?framework=mindspore)。
+
+## 产品支持情况
+
+官方 msdebug 当前文档列出了昇腾 A2、A3、310P 以及 950 系列等产品形态，但具体功能范围仍取决于 msdebug、驱动和 CANN 版本。
+
+对于 Triton 场景，还必须确认当前 Triton-Ascend 后端支持目标芯片。可以通过编译日志、Kernel Dump 中的目标信息或 Triton 后端 Target 信息确认实际架构。
+
+SIMD、SIMT、AIC、AIV、Core Dump 和局部变量打印的支持范围可能不同。本文中的功能均应以本机 msdebug 的 `help` 输出和对应版本发行说明为准。
+
+## 命令参考
+
+| 命令 | 缩写 | 说明 | Triton 示例 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `breakpoint set -f <file> -l <line>` | `b` | 设置源码行断点 | `b /data/demo/multibuffer.py:15` |
+| `run` | `r` | 启动 Python 程序 | `r` |
+| `continue` | `c` | 从断点继续运行 | `c` |
+| `print <variable>` | `p` | 打印当前 PC 可用的变量 | `p x` |
+| `frame variable` | `var` | 打印当前作用域局部变量 | `var` |
+| `memory read` | `x` | 读取 GM、UB 等内存 | `x -m UB -f float32[] 0x600 -s 128 -c 1` |
+| `thread step-over` | `n` | 单步到下一可执行源码行 | `n` |
+| `thread step-in` | `s` | 尝试进入函数 | `s` |
+| `thread step-out` | `finish` | 执行到当前函数返回 | `finish` |
+| `register read -a` | `re r -a` | 读取当前核全部可用寄存器 | `register read -a` |
+| `register read` | `re r` | 读取指定寄存器 | 见下方示例 |
+| `ascend info devices` | - | 查看 Device 信息 | `ascend info devices` |
+| `ascend info cores` | - | 查看核、PC、Block 和停止原因 | `ascend info cores` |
+| `ascend info tasks` | - | 查看 Task 信息 | `ascend info tasks` |
+| `ascend info stream` | - | 查看 Stream 信息 | `ascend info stream` |
+| `ascend info blocks` | - | 查看 Block 信息 | `ascend info blocks -d` |
+| `ascend aiv <id>` | - | 切换当前焦点 AIV | `ascend aiv 3` |
+| `ascend aic <id>` | - | 切换当前焦点 AIC | `ascend aic 17` |
+| `ascend info threads` | - | 查看 SIMT 线程 | `ascend info threads` |
+| `ascend thread <id>` | - | 切换 SIMT 线程 | `ascend thread (0,8,0)` |
+| `image add <kernel.o>` | - | 导入 Kernel 调试信息 | `image add /data/dump/hash/kernel.o` |
+| `image load -f <kernel.o> -s <slide>` | - | 按运行时偏移加载调试信息 | `image load -f /data/dump/hash/kernel.o -s 0` |
+| `thread backtrace` | `bt` | 查看调用栈，当前主要用于 Core Dump | `bt` |
+| `ascend info summary` | - | 查看 Core Dump 摘要 | `ascend info summary` |
+| `help <command>` | - | 查看本机命令帮助 | `help memory read` |
+
+读取指定寄存器时，寄存器名前需添加 `$`，例如：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) register read $PC $GPR0
+```
+
+`memory read` 常用选项：
+
+| 选项 | 含义 |
+|---|---|
+| `-m` | 内存类型，如 `GM`、`UB`、`L0A`、`L0B`、`L0C`、`L1` 等 |
+| `-f` | 显示数据类型，如 `float16[]`、`float32[]`、`int32_t[]` |
+| `-s` | 每行打印的字节数 |
+| `-c` | 打印行数 |
+| `-E` / `--offset` | 打印前跳过的元素数 |
+
+不同版本的格式名称可能略有不同，使用前执行：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) help memory read
+(msdebug) help x
+```
+
+## 工具使用
+
+### 准备 Triton 调试用例
+
+下面使用一个简单的向量加法说明。保存为 `triton_msdebug_demo.py`：
+
+```python
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+@triton.jit
+def add_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    y_ptr,
+    output_ptr,
+    n_elements,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(axis = 0)
+
+    block_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE
+    offsets = block_start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+
+    x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets)
+    y = tl.load(y_ptr + offsets)
+
+    output = x + y
+
+    tl.store(output_ptr + offsets, output)
+
+
+def vector_add(x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+    n_elements = x.numel()
+
+    output = torch.empty_like(x)
+
+    BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+
+    grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(n_elements, meta['BLOCK_SIZE']), )
+
+    add_kernel[grid](
+        x, y, output,
+        n_elements,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+
+    return output
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    a = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]
+    b = [2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0]
+
+    x = torch.tensor(a, device = 'npu')
+    y = torch.tensor(b, device = 'npu')
+
+    output_triton = vector_add(x, y)
+
+    print(output_triton)
+
+```
+
+### 启动工具
+
+```bash
+export LLVM_EXTRACT_DI_LOCAL_VARIABLES=1
+export TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO=0
+msdebug python triton_msdebug_demo.py
+```
+
+典型回显：
+
+```text
+=================================================================
+                   >>>>>   MindStudio   <<<<<
+    THE END-TO-END TOOLCHAIN TO UNLEASH HUAWEI ASCEND COMPUTE
+=================================================================
+
+msdebug 26.0.0
+(msdebug) target create "python"
+Current executable set to '/usr/local/python3.11.13/bin/python' (x86_64).
+(msdebug) settings set -- target.run-args  "multibuffer.py"
+Cannot read termcap database;
+using dumb terminal settings.
+(msdebug)
+```
+
+修改了 Triton 源码、编译常量或编译器代码后，需要重新开启强制编译并重新生成二进制。
+
+```bash
+export TRITON_ALWAYS_COMPILE=1
+```
+
+### 指定 Device ID
+
+多 Device 程序可在运行前指定调试焦点：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend device 1
+(msdebug) r
+```
+
+如果不指定，通常调试目标程序首次设置的 Device。调试用例应尽量固定 Device，避免目标 Kernel 被下发到另一个 Device。
+
+### 调试退出
+
+```text
+(msdebug) q
+Quitting LLDB will kill one or more processes. Do you really want to proceed: [Y/n] y
+```
+
+## 断点设置功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+msdebug 可以在 Triton Python Kernel 源码的指定行设置断点。设备 PC 与 Python 行号的对应关系来自 `kernel.o` 中的 DWARF 行表。
+
+### 注意事项
+
+- 建议对 `.py` 文件使用绝对路径，避免同名文件或路径改写导致错误匹配；
+- 应在 `tl.load`、实际计算、`tl.store` 等会生成设备指令的语句上设置断点；
+- 仅用于组织代码的 Python 语句、装饰器或被编译期消除的表达式不一定有设备地址；
+- Triton JIT 模块在执行 `r` 后才装载，因此运行前断点显示 pending 通常是正常现象；
+- 一条 Triton 语句可能扩展成多条地址计算、cast、memref 和 load/store 指令，断点可能解析出多个 Location；
+- `debug_line_rewriter.py`、Location 归一化 Pass 和调试 NOP 会影响最终可停位置，但 msdebug 本身不会重新生成缺失的行表。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+#### 设置行断点
+
+假设 `BREAK_X` 位于第 13 行：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) b triton_msdebug_demo.py:13
+Breakpoint 1: no locations (pending on future shared library load).
+WARNING:  Unable to resolve breakpoint to any actual locations.
+(msdebug) r
+```
+
+Kernel 完成 JIT 装载后，预期出现类似信息：
+
+```text
+[Launch of Kernel add_kernel ...]
+1 location added to breakpoint 1
+Process ... stopped
+[Switching to focus on Kernel add_kernel, CoreId ..., Type aiv]
+```
+
+pending 的含义是“当前尚未装载包含该源码行的设备模块”，不是立即失败。
+
+#### 查看断点
+
+```text
+(msdebug) breakpoint list
+```
+
+#### 删除断点
+
+```text
+(msdebug) breakpoint delete 1
+```
+
+## 内存与变量打印功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+Triton 源码中的变量可能位于寄存器、UB 或 GM，也可能只是编译器 SSA 值，没有固定内存地址。msdebug 可以在断点停止后打印当前 PC 可用的变量，并读取当前焦点核的内存。
+
+### 注意事项
+
+- `p x` 成功需要 `kernel.o` 同时包含变量 DIE 和当前 PC 有效的 Location；
+- 源码断点能命中，只能说明 `.debug_line` 有效，不能说明变量 Location 一定存在；
+- UB 是核内局部存储，切换 AIV/AIC 后，相同 UB 偏移对应另一核的数据；
+- GM 使用设备全局地址，读取前必须确认地址和长度合法；
+- 编译器可能把 Triton 变量保存在寄存器中，变量不一定拥有 UB 地址；
+- 寄存器和 UB 会在变量最后一次使用后复用；
+- `tl.load` 的 mask 为 false 时，部分 lane 的数据可能无效；
+- `-f`内存显示格式必须与真实元素类型一致,不指定默认十六进制表示；
+- 不使用`-c`指定打印行数默认为打印`4`行，不使用`-s`指定每行打印字节数默认为`128`字节。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+#### 打印指定变量
+
+```text
+(msdebug) p x
+(msdebug) p y
+(msdebug) p z
+```
+
+若变量信息可用，msdebug 会显示变量值、地址或其所在位置；如果显示 `<unavailable>`，应判断当前 PC 是否处于变量有效范围。
+
+#### 打印所有局部变量
+
+```text
+(msdebug) var
+```
+
+Triton 编译后的变量名可能与 Python 源码名不同，也可能只保留部分变量。
+
+#### 按 Triton 变量读取 UB
+
+在支持变量名解析的版本中，可以使用：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) x -m UB -f float32 x
+(msdebug) x -m UB -f float32 z -s 32
+```
+
+如果 `x` 对应一组 128 个 `float32` 元素，`-s 32` 表示每行显示 32 字节，即每行 8 个 `float32`；因此可能看到 4 行或更多行，具体总长度由变量调试信息和命令参数共同决定。
+
+#### 按已知 UB 地址读取
+
+```text
+(msdebug) x -m UB -f float32[] 0x600 -s 128 -c 1
+```
+
+该命令从当前焦点核的 UB 偏移 `0x600` 开始，按 `float32` 解释数据，每行打印 128 字节，共打印 1 行，即最多显示 32 个 `float32` 元素。
+
+#### 按已知 GM 地址读取
+
+```text
+(msdebug) x -m GM -f float32[] 0x00001240c0037000 -s 128 -c 2
+```
+
+该命令从指定 GM 地址开始，按 `float32` 格式打印两行，每行 128 字节。
+
+若需要从起始地址跳过若干元素：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) x -m GM -f float32[] 0x00001240c0037000 -s 128 -c 1 -E 16
+```
+
+#### 处理默认读取上限
+
+当读取超过默认上限时，msdebug 可能提示：
+
+```text
+Normally, 'memory read' will not read over 1024 bytes of data.
+```
+
+仅本次强制读取时，按本机 `help memory read` 中的 `--force` 选项执行；需要多次读取时，可调整：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) settings set target.max-memory-read-size 4096
+```
+
+修改上限前应先验证地址、元素类型和读取范围。
+
+#### `x`、`y`、`z` 地址与 PC 生命周期
+
+以下是一个典型而非绝对的生命周期：
+
+| 当前停点 | `x` | `y` | `z` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `tl.load(x)` 执行前 | 尚未产生 | 尚未产生 | 尚未产生 |
+| `tl.load(x)` 执行后 | 可能位于寄存器或 UB | 尚未产生 | 尚未产生 |
+| `tl.load(y)` 执行后 | 可能可用 | 可能可用 | 尚未产生 |
+| `z = x + y` 执行后 | 可能仍可用，也可能开始复用 | 可能仍可用，也可能开始复用 | 可能位于寄存器或 UB |
+| `tl.store(z)` 执行后 | 可能失效 | 可能失效 | 可能失效或只剩 GM 输出 |
+
+建议在多个连续停点分别执行：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) n
+(msdebug) p x
+(msdebug) p y
+(msdebug) p z
+(msdebug) register read -a
+```
+
+变量无法打印时，离线检查：
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-info "$KERNEL_O" | less
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loc "$KERNEL_O" | less
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loclists "$KERNEL_O" | less
+```
+
+重点查看：
+
+- 是否有对应 `DW_TAG_variable`；
+- 是否有 `DW_AT_location`；
+- Location List 的 PC 范围是否覆盖当前断点 PC；
+- Location 是寄存器、UB 地址还是其他表达式；
+- 同名变量是否属于另一个编译单元或词法作用域。
+
+如果变量 DIE 存在但没有 `DW_AT_location`，msdebug 知道变量名称，却无法恢复它当前存放的位置，此时按变量名打印失败是预期结果。
+
+官方内存命令和各选项说明可参考 [内存与变量打印](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindstudio/830/ODtools/Operatordevelopmenttools/atlasopdev_16_0067.html?framework=mindspore)。
+
+## 单步调试功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+命中源码断点后，可以使用 `n`、`s` 和 `finish` 控制当前焦点核继续执行。
+
+### 注意事项
+
+- Triton Python 函数经过内联和多级 Lowering，`s` 不一定能进入 Python 层函数；
+- 一条 Python 语句可能对应多条设备指令，同一源码行可能停止多次；
+- 多条内部 IR 也可能统一映射到同一源码行；
+- 被优化掉或没有独立设备指令的行会被跳过；
+- load/store 扩展出的 cast、memref、地址计算和调试 NOP 会影响单步停点；
+- 单步针对当前带 `*` 的焦点核，其他核可能仍停在原断点；
+- 如果 Kernel 使用同步指令，单独推进一个核可能表现为等待，应结合所有核的 PC 判断。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+#### Step Over
+
+```text
+(msdebug) b triton_msdebug_demo.py:<BREAK_X行号>
+(msdebug) r
+(msdebug) n
+```
+
+执行后查看所有核状态：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+```
+
+当前核的 `stop reason` 应显示 `step over` 或仍显示同时命中的 breakpoint。
+
+#### Step In
+
+```text
+(msdebug) s
+```
+
+如果后端已将函数内联，`s` 可能表现为移动到同一函数中的下一个有效 Location，而不是进入新的 Python 栈帧。
+
+#### Step Out
+
+```text
+(msdebug) finish
+```
+
+对于完全内联的 Triton Kernel，可能不存在可见的独立调用帧，此命令的效果取决于最终 DWARF 调用信息。
+
+#### 判断是重复执行还是行号重复
+
+如果 `n` 多次停在同一源码行，结合当前 PC 和反汇编判断：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) re r $PC
+(msdebug) disassemble
+```
+
+同时离线查看：
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-line "$KERNEL_O"
+```
+
+只要 PC 在变化，通常说明调试器正在执行映射到同一源码行的不同设备指令，并不代表 Python 语句被重复运行。
+
+## 中断运行功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+当 Triton Kernel 长时间不返回时，可通过 `Ctrl+C` 中断在 msdebug 内启动的程序，查看当前停止位置。
+
+### 注意事项
+
+- 只能中断由当前 msdebug 会话启动的程序；
+- 卡住可能来自 Kernel 死循环、核间同步、等待事件或错误的控制流；
+- 根据官方当前约束，`Ctrl+C` 中断后主要支持调试信息展示和核切换；单步、寄存器读取、变量/内存打印和 `continue` 可能不可用；
+- 因此，`Ctrl+C` 主要用于确认各核卡在什么位置，而不是替代普通断点调试。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+```text
+(msdebug) r
+<按 Ctrl+C>
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks -d
+```
+
+观察是否出现：
+
+- 某个核 PC 长时间不变；
+- 多个核停在同步或等待位置；
+- 某个 Block 未到达与其他 Block 相同的阶段；
+- 当前源码位置落在 Triton 循环或 load/store 等待附近。
+
+完成信息收集后退出：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) q
+```
+
+## 核切换功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+将调试焦点切换到指定 AIV 或 AIC。切换后，源码位置、寄存器以及 UB 等局部内存操作都针对新焦点核。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+查看当前核：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+```
+
+切换到 AIV 3：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend aiv 3
+```
+
+切换到 AIC 17：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend aic 17
+```
+
+再次确认焦点：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+```
+
+输出中带 `*` 的行是当前焦点核。
+
+### Triton 多 Block 场景说明
+
+Triton 的 `program_id`/Block 会被调度到设备核执行。查询映射：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks -d
+```
+
+读取分核数据前，应先执行：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend aiv <core-id>
+(msdebug) p x
+(msdebug) x -m UB -f float32 x
+```
+
+切换到另一个 AIV 后再次读取，即可比较不同 Block/核的数据。两个核即使都显示 `UB 0x600`，也代表各自核的局部 UB 数据，不是同一物理上下文。
+
+官方核切换示例可参考 [Vector 算子调试示例](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindstudio/830/ODtools/Operatordevelopmenttools/atlasopdev_16_0074.html?framework=mindspore)。
+
+## 检查程序状态功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+在普通断点或单步停点，可以读取当前焦点核的寄存器，确认 PC、通用寄存器及状态寄存器。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+读取全部可用寄存器：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) register read -a
+```
+
+读取指定寄存器：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) register read $PC $GPR0 $GPR30
+```
+
+也可使用缩写：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) re r $PC
+```
+
+对 Triton 问题，优先关注：
+
+- `PC`：与 `.debug_line`、反汇编及变量 Location List 对照；
+- 通用寄存器：分析地址计算、循环索引或指针；
+- 状态和事件寄存器：分析 Kernel 等待或同步问题；
+- 切核后的寄存器差异：判断是否只有单个 Block/核异常。
+
+寄存器名无效时会返回相应错误，应使用 `register read -a` 确认当前芯片和核类型实际支持的名称。
+
+## 调试信息展示功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+查询当前 Kernel 所在的 Device、Stream、Task、Block、核和停止原因。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+#### Device 信息
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info devices
+```
+
+`*` 表示当前焦点 Device。常见字段包括 Device ID、AIC/AIV 数量和核 Mask。
+
+#### 核信息
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+```
+
+重点字段：
+
+| 字段 | Triton 调试含义 |
+|---|---|
+| `CoreId` | 当前 AIC/AIV 的核 ID |
+| `Type` | 核类型，通常为 `aic` 或 `aiv` |
+| `Device` | 逻辑 Device ID |
+| `Stream` | Kernel 下发所在 Stream |
+| `Task` | 当前 Stream 中的 Task |
+| `Block` | Triton program/Block 对应的逻辑 Block ID |
+| `PC` | 当前核设备 PC |
+| `stop reason` | breakpoint、step over、step in、Ctrl+C 或异常类型等 |
+| `Filename/Line` | PC 对应的 Triton 源文件和行号，无法映射时可能为 `NA` |
+
+#### Task 信息
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info tasks
+```
+
+用于确认当前 Task 对应的 Kernel Invocation，特别适合一个 Python 脚本调用多个 Kernel 时筛选目标。
+
+#### Stream 信息
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info stream
+```
+
+用于确认目标 Kernel 所在的 Stream 和核类型。
+
+#### Block 信息
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks -d
+```
+
+`-d` 会显示所有 Block 当前停止位置，适合排查多核不同步、某个 Block 路径异常以及分核数据差异。
+
+## SIMT 线程切换功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+如果目标 Triton Kernel 在当前芯片和后端上以受 msdebug 支持的 SIMT 方式执行，可以查询并切换 SIMT 线程。SIMD Kernel 或不支持 SIMT 调试的版本不适用本节。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+查询线程：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info threads
+```
+
+查询或切换线程：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend thread 100
+(msdebug) ascend thread (0,8,0)
+```
+
+切换线程后，源码位置和变量上下文会变化。应重新确认：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info threads
+(msdebug) var
+```
+
+若命令不受支持或没有线程信息，应先确认 Kernel 编程模式、芯片和 msdebug 版本，而不是把它判断为 Triton 行号问题。
+
+## 解析异常算子 Dump 文件功能介绍
+
+### 功能说明
+
+NPU 发生硬件异常时，可以生成异常算子 Core Dump，离线恢复异常核、PC、寄存器和部分内存现场。此功能适用于在线断点无法稳定复现或程序已经异常退出的场景。
+
+### 注意事项
+
+- 开启异常算子 Dump 后，不应同时使用在线 msdebug；
+- 必须尽量使用异常现场完全匹配的 `kernel.o`；
+- Python 源码相同不代表二进制相同，Block Size、Autotune、编译器版本和后端选项都会改变二进制；
+- 硬件可能在产生异常后继续执行若干指令再上报，因此 Core 中部分内存和寄存器可能不是最初故障瞬间的值；
+- 异常 PC 通常比普通数据更可靠，应先从 PC、停止原因和反汇编开始；
+- 官方当前说明中，`bt` 主要用于 Core Dump，且只在部分硬件异常停止原因下保证准确性。
+
+### 使用示例
+
+#### 生成异常算子 Core 文件
+
+在线 msdebug 退出后，在普通终端设置：
+
+```bash
+export ASCEND_DUMP_SCENE=aic_err_detail_dump
+export ASCEND_DUMP_PATH=/data/ascend_core_dump
+mkdir -p "$ASCEND_DUMP_PATH"
+python triton_msdebug_demo.py
+```
+
+只有触发相应设备异常时才会生成 `.core` 文件。
+
+#### 加载 Core 文件和 `kernel.o`
+
+```bash
+msdebug --core /data/ascend_core_dump/<error>.core \
+  /data/triton_msdebug_dump/<hash>/kernel.o
+```
+
+如果暂时没有二进制，也可以只加载 Core：
+
+```bash
+msdebug --core /data/ascend_core_dump/<error>.core
+```
+
+但缺少匹配 `kernel.o` 时，源码行、符号和调用栈解析会受到限制。
+
+#### 查看异常摘要
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend info summary
+(msdebug) ascend info devices
+(msdebug) ascend info cores
+(msdebug) ascend info blocks -d
+```
+
+#### 切换异常核
+
+```text
+(msdebug) ascend aiv <id>
+(msdebug) ascend aic <id>
+```
+
+选择 `stop reason` 为 `MTE_ERROR`、`VEC_ERROR`、`CUBE_ERROR` 等异常的核，然后查看：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) bt
+(msdebug) frame select 0
+(msdebug) register read -a
+```
+
+#### 根据 PC 定位指令
+
+```text
+(msdebug) re r $PC
+(msdebug) image list -o -f
+(msdebug) image lookup -a <pc-address>
+(msdebug) disassemble -s <start-address> -e <end-address>
+```
+
+#### 读取 Core 中内存
+
+根据 `ascend info summary` 输出的内存段和当前核读取：
+
+```text
+(msdebug) x -m GM -f uint8_t[] <address> -s 128 -c 1
+(msdebug) x -m STACK -f uint8_t[] <address> -s 128 -c 1
+(msdebug) x -m DCACHE -f uint8_t[] <address> -s 128 -c 1
+```
+
+具体支持的 Core Dump 内存类型应以 `help memory read` 为准。
+
+## 常见问题
+
+### msdebug 初始化失败并提示 `0x20102`
+
+典型信息：
+
+```text
+msdebug failed to initialize, please run "echo 1 > /proc/debug_switch"
+```
+
+检查：
+
+```bash
+echo 1 > /proc/debug_switch
+cat /proc/debug_switch
+ls -l /dev/drv_debug
+```
+
+容器中无法修改时应回到宿主机处理。
+
+### 断点命中，但 `var` 没有变量
+
+断点使用 `.debug_line`，变量使用 `.debug_info` 和 `.debug_loc*`。按以下顺序检查：
+
+```bash
+echo "$LLVM_EXTRACT_DI_LOCAL_VARIABLES"
+echo "$TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO"
+llvm-dwarfdump --verify "$KERNEL_O"
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-info "$KERNEL_O" | less
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loc "$KERNEL_O" | less
+```
+
+如果变量存在但没有 Location，或当前 PC 不在 Location List 范围内，msdebug 无法打印该变量。
+
+### 可以用 msdebug 给 `NormalizeDebugLineLocations.cpp` 下断点吗
+
+不可以。它是主机侧 MLIR Pass，应使用编译日志、Pass 前后 IR、GDB/LLDB 调试 `triton-opt`。msdebug 调试的是已经装载到 NPU 的 `kernel.o`。
+
+### 读出的 UB 数据不符合预期
+
+依次检查：
+
+1. `ascend info cores` 中的焦点核是否正确；
+2. 是否在 `tl.load` 完成后、内存复用前停止；
+3. 数据类型和 `-f` 是否一致；
+4. `-s` 是否按字节理解；
+5. mask 是否使部分 lane 无效；
+6. Block Size 和实际向量长度是否一致；
+7. 是否正在调试另一份 Autotune Kernel；
+8. 地址是 UB 偏移还是 GM 绝对地址。
+
+### `LD_PRELOAD detected` 是否需要处理
+
+该警告单独出现时通常不是失败原因。如果 msdebug 后续可以初始化、命中断点并读取设备信息，可以先保留当前环境。只有发生库冲突、符号加载失败或进程初始化失败时，再核对 `LD_PRELOAD` 指向的库。
+
+## 附录：`kernel.o` 调试信息检查
+
+### 检查 Section
+
+```bash
+readelf -S "$KERNEL_O" | grep -E 'debug|symtab|strtab'
+```
+
+### 校验 DWARF
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --verify "$KERNEL_O"
+```
+
+### 查看行表
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-line "$KERNEL_O" | less
+```
+
+### 查看编译单元和变量
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-info "$KERNEL_O" | less
+```
+
+### 查看变量位置
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loc "$KERNEL_O" | less
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loclists "$KERNEL_O" | less
+```
+
+### 保存分析结果
+
+```bash
+llvm-dwarfdump --verify "$KERNEL_O" > dwarf-verify.txt 2>&1
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-info "$KERNEL_O" > dwarf-info.txt
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-line "$KERNEL_O" > dwarf-line.txt
+llvm-dwarfdump --debug-loc "$KERNEL_O" > dwarf-locations.txt
+```
+
+提交 Triton-Ascend 调试问题时，建议同时提供最小 Python 用例、版本信息、环境变量、完全匹配的 `kernel.o`、上述 DWARF 输出、msdebug 会话日志、目标 Device/核/Block 和实际停止 PC。
+
+## 参考资料
+
+- [MindStudio Debugger 用户指南](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msdebug/blob/master/docs/zh/user_guide/msdebug_user_guide.md)
+- [MindStudio Debugger 工具概述](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindstudio/830/ODtools/Operatordevelopmenttools/atlasopdev_16_0062.html?framework=mindspore)
+- [Cuda-gdb官方文档](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-gdb/index.html#single-stepping)
+- [DWARF location list 说明](https://dwarfstd.org/doc/040408.1.html)
+- [LLVM 调试变量说明](https://llvm.org/docs/SourceLevelDebugging.html)

+"""Does a runtime scalar divisible by 16 specialize and force a recompile?
+
+Mechanism (``python/src/specialize.cc``, ``handle_long_type``): an i32 scalar
+specializes to ``("i32", "D")`` when ``(value & 15) == 0`` and alignment
+specialization is enabled, otherwise to ``("i32", "")``. The flag ``align`` in
+the binder comes from ``backend.use_alignment_specialization(options)``, which
+the Ascend backend enables only for ``compile_mode="simt_only"`` (default
+``"simd"`` keeps it off, see ``third_party/ascend/backend/compiler.py``).
+
+So on Ascend (simd) a multiple of 16 and a non-multiple share the key ``""``:
+crossing the 16-byte boundary does NOT recompile. The test reports the real
+specialization key observed on each launch (``kernel.src.signature``), the
+kernel-load count per reuse mode, and what the keys would be if alignment
+specialization were turned on (``simt_only``).
+
+Unlike ``SCALE`` in ``test_scale_reuse.py``, the scalar under test is a runtime
+argument, not a constexpr, so the constexpr-reuse feature (mode 1/2) does not
+dynamicize it: all three modes must observe the same load count.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from triton._C.libtriton import native_specialize_impl
+from triton.backends.compiler import BaseBackend
+
+from reuse_common import reuse_mode
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def add_value(out_ptr, x_ptr, n, value, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    offsets = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < n
+    x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=0)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, x + value, mask=mask)
+
+
+def launch_add(value, x, out, tile=64):
+    """Launch ``add_value`` with one runtime scalar and check the result."""
+    n = x.numel()
+    kernel = add_value[(triton.cdiv(n, tile), )](out, x, n, value, BLOCK=tile)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    expected = x + torch.tensor(value, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected, rtol=0, atol=0, check_dtype=True)
+    return kernel
+
+
+def _specialize_key(value, align):
+    """The cache-key fragment native_specialize_impl computes for a scalar int."""
+    return native_specialize_impl(BaseBackend, value, False, True, align)[1]
+
+
+def test_scalar_divisible_by_16_specialization(reuse_mode):
+    mode, loads = reuse_mode
+    values = [16, 17, 32, 33, 48, 64]  # cross the 16-byte boundary repeatedly
+    n, tile = 1024, 64
+    x = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+
+    kernels = []
+    for value in values:
+        kernel = launch_add(value, x, out, tile)
+        kernels.append(kernel)
+        key = kernel.src.signature["value"][1]  # observed specialization key
+        print(
+            f"[reuse_mode={mode}] value={value:3d} spec_key={key!r} "
+            f"kernel=0x{id(kernel):x} loads_so_far={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    distinct = len({id(k) for k in kernels})
+    print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] summary: distinct_kernels={distinct} kernel_loads={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    keys_aligned = sorted({_specialize_key(v, True) for v in values})
+    keys_ascend = sorted({_specialize_key(v, False) for v in values})
+    print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] specialize_impl keys: align=True -> {keys_aligned}; "
+          f"align=False -> {keys_ascend}", flush=True)
+    assert keys_aligned == ["", "D"], "16|32|48|64 must key 'D' and 17|33 '' with alignment specialization on"
+    assert keys_ascend == [""], "Ascend simd disables alignment specialization; all values must key ''"
+
+    # Ascend default simd: alignment specialization is off, so every value gets
+    # the same key and a single kernel is loaded - 16-divisibility does NOT
+    # recompile. With simt_only the boundary would produce two loads.
+    assert len(loads) == 1, (f"values crossing the 16-byte boundary must reuse one kernel under simd "
+                             f"(got {len(loads)} loads, expected 1); simt_only would split into "
+                             f"{len(keys_aligned)} specializations -> {len(keys_aligned)} loads")
+    assert distinct == 1

+"""Device-level observation tests: does changing constexpr SCALE recompile ``scale``?
+
+Run on an NPU with a patched triton-ascend build (the JIT reuse handoff must be
+present, see ``patch/triton-ascend-3.6.0.patch``)::
+
+    python -m pytest -q -s third_party/ascend/unittest/reuse_ut/test_scale_reuse.py
+
+The test launches the same ``scale``-based kernel with different constexpr
+``SCALE`` values and reports, per launch, how many distinct kernels were really
+loaded:
+
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=0`` (disabled): every new ``SCALE`` is a
+  new specialized variant, so it recompiles and reloads -> one load per SCALE.
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=1``: ``SCALE`` is dynamicized into a
+  runtime argument -> all SCALE values share one kernel -> a single load.
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=2``: same single-load contract plus the
+  optional tile reuse / background compilation machinery.
+
+Kernel loads are counted with ``triton.knobs.runtime.kernel_load_start_hook``
+(fires exactly once per loaded ``CompiledKernel``). Unlike ``jit_cache_hook``,
+this hook does NOT disable the reuse path. With ``-s`` you also see the
+``[ascend-reuse]`` diagnostics on stderr (analysis decisions and dispatch
+outcomes) when reuse is enabled.
+
+The parametrized modes share one pytest process, so the fixture resets the
+global ``ReuseHandler`` per run: its registry and the private owner's device
+cache would otherwise leak an already-loaded variant into the next mode (an
+"exact ready" hit that loads nothing).
+
+The kernel, launch helper and the ``reuse_mode`` fixture are defined here; the
+fixture itself is shared via ``reuse_common.py``.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from reuse_common import reuse_mode
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def scale(x, SCALE: tl.constexpr):
+    return x * SCALE
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def scale_kernel(out_ptr, x_ptr, n, SCALE: tl.constexpr, TILE: tl.constexpr):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    offsets = pid * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE)
+    mask = offsets < n
+    x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    y = scale(x, SCALE)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, y, mask=mask)
+
+
+def launch_scale(scale_value, x, out, tile=64):
+    n = x.numel()
+    kernel = scale_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, tile), )](out, x, n, SCALE=scale_value, TILE=tile)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, x * scale_value)
+    return kernel
+
+
+def test_scale_constexpr_changes_and_recompilation(reuse_mode):
+    mode, loads = reuse_mode
+    n, tile = 1024, 64
+    x = torch.randn(n, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+
+    scales = [1, 2, 3, 4]
+    kernels = []
+    for scale_value in scales:
+        kernel = launch_scale(scale_value, x, out, tile)
+        kernels.append(kernel)
+        print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] SCALE={scale_value} -> kernel=0x{id(kernel):x} "
+              f"loads_so_far={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    distinct = len({id(k) for k in kernels})
+    print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] summary: distinct_kernels={distinct} kernel_loads={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    if mode == 0:
+        assert len(loads) == len(scales), (
+            f"mode 0 must recompile for every SCALE (got {len(loads)} loads, expected {len(scales)})")
+        assert distinct == len(scales)
+    else:
+        assert len(loads) == 1, (
+            f"mode {mode} must reuse a single kernel for every SCALE (got {len(loads)} loads, expected 1). "
+            "If the runtime handoff patch is missing, reuse never activates; check that "
+            "AscendBackend.get_jit_reuse_handler is reachable in the installed triton.")
+        assert distinct == 1

+"""Does a constexpr TILE change recompile when tile reuse is enabled?
+
+Run on an NPU with a patched triton-ascend build::
+
+    python -m pytest -q -s third_party/ascend/unittest/reuse_ut/test_tile_reuse.py
+
+The kernel is a plain copy indexed by ``pid * TILE + arange(TILE)`` (the same
+shape as ``copy_kernel`` in ``test_constexpr_reuse.py``). ``N`` is a constexpr
+that mode 2 dynamicizes into a runtime argument; ``TILE`` is proven as a
+*schedule* parameter (``ParameterClass.ScheduleReusable``) and stays constexpr
+in the compiled variant.
+
+Per mode:
+
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=0`` (disabled): every ``TILE`` value is
+  its own specialized variant -> one load per TILE.
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=1``: ``TILE`` stays a compile-time
+  specialization (tile reuse is not proven without mode 2) -> one load per
+  TILE again.
+* ``TRITON_ASCEND_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_REUSE=2``: tile reuse. The first ``TILE``
+  compiles and loads one kernel; a later ``TILE`` is *scheduled* onto it
+  (``adapt_tile``/``adapt_grid`` re-derive the runtime TILE override and the
+  grid that preserves full coverage) -> a single load, no recompile.
+
+Kernel loads are counted with ``triton.knobs.runtime.kernel_load_start_hook``
+as in the sibling tests. With ``-s`` the ``[ascend-reuse]`` diagnostics show
+the ``schedule-reused=[TILE: ...]`` dispatch.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from reuse_common import reuse_mode
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def copy_kernel(src, dst, N: tl.constexpr, TILE: tl.constexpr):
+    index = tl.program_id(0) * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE)
+    value = tl.load(src + index, mask=index < N, other=0)
+    tl.store(dst + index, value, mask=index < N)
+
+
+def launch_copy(n, tile, src, dst):
+    """Launch ``copy_kernel`` with one TILE and check the copy result."""
+    # The grid contract is cdiv(N, TILE); dispatch recomputes it when it
+    # schedules the launch onto a kernel compiled with a different TILE.
+    grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(meta["N"], meta["TILE"]), )
+    kernel = copy_kernel[grid](src, dst, N=n, TILE=tile)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst, src)
+    return kernel
+
+
+def test_tile_change_reuses_loaded_kernel(reuse_mode):
+    mode, loads = reuse_mode
+    n = 1000
+    src = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+
+    tiles = [64, 32, 128]  # cross the TILE boundary; later tiles must reuse the first kernel
+    kernels = []
+    for tile in tiles:
+        kernel = launch_copy(n, tile, src, dst)
+        kernels.append(kernel)
+        print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] TILE={tile} -> kernel=0x{id(kernel):x} "
+              f"loads_so_far={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    distinct = len({id(k) for k in kernels})
+    print(f"[reuse_mode={mode}] summary: distinct_kernels={distinct} kernel_loads={len(loads)}", flush=True)
+
+    if mode == 2:
+        # Tile reuse is proven only in mode 2: TILE is a schedule parameter, so
+        # every later TILE is dispatched onto the already-loaded kernel and the
+        # grid is re-derived to preserve coverage. No new load fires.
+        assert len(loads) == 1, (
+            f"mode 2 must schedule every TILE onto one loaded kernel (got {len(loads)} loads, expected 1). "
+            "If the runtime handoff patch or the compile worker is missing, tile reuse never activates.")
+        assert distinct == 1
+    else:
+        # Modes 0/1 keep TILE a compile-time specialization: each TILE value
+        # produces its own specialized variant and recompiles.
+        assert len(loads) == len(tiles), (
+            f"mode {mode} must recompile for every TILE (got {len(loads)} loads, expected {len(tiles)})")
+        assert distinct == len(tiles)

[ascend](feat) TLA: device print/assert and cube pipeline alignment (#2810)

* [ascend](feat) add tla.device_print emitting hivm.hir.debug directly

Motivation: the original tla.device_print reused tl.device_print (plain
tt.print), which only accepts TT_Type operands; the pure-buffer interface
set has no scalar-extraction op, so a UB buffer element could not be
printed at the buffer stage (a buffer_access is not convertible to a
tensor, and there is no scalar-extraction op to make one).
Design: emit hivm.hir.debug directly from the TLA frontend with debugtype
"print" (the hfusion.print -> hivm.hir.debug convention), whose operand
accepts AnyInteger/AnyFloat/TensorOrMemref: UB buffers and buf[i0, i1, ...]
element ranges (lowered to a 0-d subview) can be printed at the buffer
stage.  Merge device_print.py and device_assert.py into tla/debug.py; bind
create_hivm_debug in tla_builder.cc and mount it via setup_unified_builder.
Keep the inside-scope / non-UB rejection, and update the tla_ut device_print
test to assert hivm.hir.debug at both the AST and lowered stages.
Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](refactor) align TLA cube kernels with the npuir pipeline

- accept physical 4-D NZ shapes in tla.copy and tla.mmad (gemm tests updated)
- drop the unused is_mem_unique alloc option
- pin hivm.vf_mode<SIMD> on simd scopes

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) infer TLA kernel core type from scopes

Classify single-kernel TLA modules as AIC, AIV or MIX in Python using scope core-mode markers. Stamp hivm.func_core_type and keep mix_mode consistent, leaving unscoped kernels to backend inference.

Validation: not run as requested.

* [ascend](feat) dump final ttadapter IR via TLA_IR_DUMP_DIR

Motivation: tla_ut IR tests need a quick, device-free way to inspect the
final IR handed to npuir; dumping every intermediate stage was noise.
Design: lower_offline writes only 01_linalg.mlir (the ttadapter boundary)
under $TLA_IR_DUMP_DIR/<kernel>/.  The entry func name is read before
lowering because the pass manager rewrites the module in place
(tt.func -> func.func); explicit output_dir keeps the original per-stage
dump behavior in compile_offline.
Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](refactor) centralize TLA buffer space vocabulary in core.py

Motivation: buffer-space checks were spread as hardcoded strings (the
buffer_type validation tuple and duplicated "ub" comparisons in
device_print), and a draft IR-type string match silently failed because
IR values expose get_type() rather than a .type attribute.
Design: core.py now defines the single space vocabulary (SPACES, with
the HIVM mnemonic reverse map used by tla_builder.cc) and exposes
space_of()/is_ub(); buffer_type validation and device_print's UB checks
are rewritten on top of them.  Semantic dispatch in copy/cube/alloc/view
keeps comparing the frontend enum, now backed by SPACES.
Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add tla.scope.vector for vector-core regions

Motivation: TLA needs a vector-core container that hosts non-SIMD ops
(GM<->UB copies) and nests tla.scope.simd() VFs, matching the affinity
canonical input (outer VECTOR scope wrapping DMA + an outlined SIMD VF).

Design: expose the base scope class as tla.scope.vector; it stamps only
hivm.tcore_type<VECTOR> plus tla.core_mode="vector" (no VF markers), so
outline-scope never extracts it and InlineScope(forceInline) folds it
back at the end of the HIVM pipeline. Register it in TLA_WITH_DISPATCH;
simd scopes keep their VF markers whether nested or standalone. Add 5
IR/compile tests (scope/): copy_only (DMA-only vector scope), simd_only
(standalone simd regression), nested_simd (vector wrapping simd),
multi_vf (two sibling simd scopes in one vector scope), gm2l1 (GM->L1
nd2nz inside a vector scope, IR-only fragment).

Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add TLA sync interfaces

Add tla.sync split into per-op builder bindings (barrier, set_flag,
wait_flag, sync_all, block_set_flag, block_wait_flag) with shared pipe
validation and core-type inference in the builder.

Tests live under tla_ut/sync and follow the 3-stage case template:
- sync_intra: out = a + b with hand-inserted MTE2->V->MTE3 pipeline
  synchronization, barrier and sync_all, verified end to end.
- sync_inter: cube gemm handoff to the vector core through an FFTS flag,
  verified end to end.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add TLA inter-core sync tests and tla.simd.vexp

Motivation: gemm_bias had a real data race on shared UB - the AIC
fixpipe writes c_ub while the AIV vload reads it with no ordering - and
softmax needs elementwise exp on the AIV core, which the TLA frontend
did not expose. Both need test coverage for the hand-inserted
inter-core (AIC <-> AIV) synchronization pattern where intra-core
ordering is left to the compiler.
Design: fix gemm_bias by raising flag 0 on PIPE_FIX in the cube scope
after fixpipe and waiting on PIPE_V in the vector scope before the SIMD
stage, which also hosts the nested SIMD VF and the UB->GM store. Add an
"exp" branch to the TLA unary builder (hivmave::VFExpOp) and a
tla.simd.vexp wrapper; add a single-tile flash-attention forward test
(Q@K^T softmax @ V) signaling three handoff flags (S/P/O), with the
softmax row loop in tl.range and the run stage checked against a torch
reference.
Risks: mmad with f32 inputs passes IR verification, but hardware support
needs real-device validation.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](chore) format TLA sync and flash-attn sources

Reformat C++/Python touched by the TLA sync and flash-attention work
(clang-format / black style). No behavior change.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](refactor) drop bare tla.core_mode scope attribute

Motivation: the TLA scope classes already stamp the dialect attribute
code_generator and read back by compiler.infer_func_core_type, duplicating
the same information under a non-dialect attribute name. Bare frontend keys
have already caused silent core-type mismatches in bishengir passes (the
tcore_type incident), so the redundant second source should be removed.
Design: delete the "tla.core_mode" write in handle_scope_with and infer
AIC/AIV/MIX in infer_func_core_type from the printed #hivm.tcore_type<...>
attribute (the binding exposes no generic attribute reader). Update the
nested_simd / copy_only IR assertions accordingly.
Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

+"""tla.device_print / tla.device_assert: device diagnostics.
+
+``device_print`` emits ``hivm.hir.debug`` directly instead of ``tt.print``
+(``tt.print`` only takes TT_Type operands and the pure-buffer interface set has
+no scalar-extraction op): a UB buffer/memref or a ``buf[i0, i1, ...]`` element
+range (lowered to a 0-d subview) can be printed at the buffer stage.  Only
+allowed outside ``tla.scope`` and on UB-backed values.
+
+``device_assert`` mirrors ``tl.device_assert``: emitted only under
+``options.debug`` (else no-op).  The condition must be a scalar i1 — the
+pure-buffer interface set cannot derive one from vector registers, so vector
+conditions are rejected to keep the ``tensor<``-free IR contract.
+"""
+
+from triton.language.core import _unwrap_if_constexpr
+from triton.language.core import builtin
+
+from .core import buffer
+from .core import buffer_access
+from .core import is_ub
+from .core import space_of
+
+__all__ = ["device_assert", "device_print"]
+

+def _in_scope(generator):
+    """True when codegen is inside a ``scope.scope`` body.
+
+    The bindings expose ``block -> region`` and ``op -> region`` but not
+    ``region -> parent op``, so the owning scope is found by a module scan.
+    """
+    region_id = generator.builder.get_insertion_block().get_parent().id()
+    found = [False]
+
+    def visit(op):
+        # scope.scope is single-region (SingleBlock in ScopeOps.td).
+        if op.get_name() == "scope.scope" and op.get_region(0).id() == region_id:
+            found[0] = True
+
+    generator.module.walk(visit)
+    return found[0]
+
+

+    """Map a tla value to an ``hivm.hir.debug`` operand.
+
+    ``buffer_access`` -> 0-d memref subview (only the addressed element),
+    UB ``buffer`` -> the memref itself, scalar -> tensor handle.  Non-UB
+    spaces (L1/GM) are rejected: the debug chain prints UB-backed values only.
+    """
+    if isinstance(arg, buffer_access):
+        src = arg.buffer
+        if not is_ub(src):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"tla.device_print: only UB values are supported, got {space_of(src)}")

+        rank = len(src.shape)
+        return builder.create_tla_subview(src.handle, offsets, [1] * rank, [1] * rank)
+    if isinstance(arg, buffer):
+        if not is_ub(arg):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"tla.device_print: only UB values are supported, got {space_of(arg)}")
+        return arg.handle

+"""Explicit Ascend synchronization: intra-core pipes and cross-core flags.
+
+Pipelines are compile-time strings, e.g. ``"V"`` or ``"PIPE_MTE2"``.
+Event IDs are compile-time integers in [0, 7]; cross-core flag IDs are in
+[0, 15]. ``sync_all`` uses the backend's default global synchronization flags.
+
+Cross-core flags are emitted as ``hivm.hir.sync_block_set/wait`` with an
+explicit synchronization mode, which bishengir lowers to the FFTS
+``SET.CROSS.CORE`` / ``WAIT.FLAG.DEV`` instructions. The A5 per-vector-core
+``block_inter_*`` pair is not exposed yet, and the buffer-token instructions
+(``get_buf``/``rls_buf``) have no backend operation.
+"""
+
+from triton.language.core import builtin, _unwrap_if_constexpr
+
+__all__ = ["barrier", "set_flag", "wait_flag", "sync_all", "block_set_flag", "block_wait_flag"]
+
+_PIPES = frozenset([
+    "PIPE_S",
+    "PIPE_V",
+    "PIPE_M",
+    "PIPE_MTE1",
+    "PIPE_MTE2",
+    "PIPE_MTE3",
+    "PIPE_ALL",
+    "PIPE_MTE4",
+    "PIPE_MTE5",
+    "PIPE_V2",
+    "PIPE_FIX",
+])
+
+
+def _pipe(pipe):
+    """Normalize a compile-time pipeline name and check it is known."""
+    pipe = _unwrap_if_constexpr(pipe)
+    if not isinstance(pipe, str):
+        raise TypeError("pipe must be a compile-time string")
+    pipe = pipe.upper()
+    pipe = pipe if pipe.startswith("PIPE_") else "PIPE_" + pipe
+    if pipe not in _PIPES:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown synchronization pipe: {pipe}")
+    return pipe
+
+
+def _integer(value, name, maximum):
+    """Check a compile-time integer lies in the hardware range [0, maximum]."""
+    value = _unwrap_if_constexpr(value)
+    if type(value) is not int:
+        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a compile-time integer")
+    if not 0 <= value <= maximum:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be in [0, {maximum}], got {value}")
+    return value
+
+
+@builtin
+def barrier(pipe, _semantic=None):
+    """Wait for all preceding instructions on a pipeline."""
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_barrier(_pipe(pipe))
+
+
+@builtin
+def set_flag(pipe1, pipe2, event_id, _semantic=None):
+    """Signal completion from producer ``pipe1`` to consumer ``pipe2``."""
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_set_flag(_pipe(pipe1), _pipe(pipe2), _integer(event_id, "event_id", 7))
+
+
+@builtin
+def wait_flag(pipe1, pipe2, event_id, _semantic=None):
+    """Consume the event sent from producer ``pipe1`` to consumer ``pipe2``."""
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_wait_flag(_pipe(pipe1), _pipe(pipe2), _integer(event_id, "event_id", 7))
+
+
+@builtin
+def sync_all(mode, _semantic=None):
+    """Hardware global barrier: False synchronizes AIV, True all AIC/AIV."""
+    mode = _unwrap_if_constexpr(mode)
+    if type(mode) is not bool:
+        raise TypeError("sync_all mode must be a compile-time bool")
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_sync_all(mode)
+
+
+@builtin
+def block_set_flag(mode, pipe, flag, _semantic=None):
+    """
+    Signal a cross-core flag from the current core.
+
+    :param mode: 0 = inter-block, 1 = inter-subblock, 2 = intra-block
+    :param pipe: signalling pipeline
+    :param flag: flag ID in [0, 15]
+    """
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_block_set_flag(_integer(mode, "mode", 2), _pipe(pipe), _integer(flag, "flag", 15))
+
+
+@builtin
+def block_wait_flag(pipe, flag, _semantic=None):
+    """
+    Wait for a cross-core flag on the given pipeline.
+
+    :param pipe: waiting pipeline
+    :param flag: flag ID in [0, 15], matching :func:`block_set_flag`
+    """
+    _semantic.builder.create_tla_block_wait_flag(_pipe(pipe), _integer(flag, "flag", 15))

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: single-tile flash-attention forward.
+
+Semantics: O[BM, N] = softmax(Q[BM, D] @ K[BN, D]^T / sqrt(D)) @ V[BN, N]
+
+Inter-core (AIC <-> AIV) handoffs are synchronized by explicit FFTS flags
+(``tla.sync.block_set_flag`` / ``block_wait_flag``); intra-core ordering
+is left to the compiler.  Three flags, one per handoff:
+
+  FLAG_S : AIC fixpipe wrote S to UB  -> AIV softmax reads S
+  FLAG_P : AIV stored P to GM         -> AIC loads P back into L1
+  FLAG_O : AIC fixpipe wrote O to UB  -> AIV stores O to GM
+
+P must round-trip through GM because there is no UB -> L1 path yet; it is
+kept f32 (softmax output) and V is fp32 so both mmad inputs share dtype.
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline HIVM/AVE IR structure (2 mmadL1 / 2 fixpipe / 4 nd2nz,
+            3 sync set+wait, 2 stores, exp in the softmax row loop)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist
+  run     : real-device launch + accuracy (FLASH_ATTN OK vs torch reference)
+
+v1 scope: single tile (BM x BN x D), no K-loop / causal mask.
+"""
+import sys, os
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))  # tests/
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+# BM query rows, BN key/value rows, D feature dim, N output cols.
+SHAPE = dict(BM=64, BN=64, D=128, N=64, FLAG_S=0, FLAG_P=1, FLAG_O=2)
+
+SIGNATURE = {"Q_ptr": "*fp16", "K_ptr": "*fp16", "V_ptr": "*fp32", "P_ptr": "*fp32", "O_ptr": "*fp32"}
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def flash_attn(Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, P_ptr, O_ptr, BM: tl.constexpr, BN: tl.constexpr, D: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr,
+               SCALE: tl.constexpr, FLAG_S: tl.constexpr, FLAG_P: tl.constexpr, FLAG_O: tl.constexpr):
+    tl.static_assert(D % 16 == 0 and BM % 16 == 0 and BN % 16 == 0 and N % 16 == 0,
+                     "BM/BN/D/N must be multiples of 16 (cube tile)")
+    tl.static_assert(BN == 64, "v1: softmax row must fit one 64-lane f32 register")
+
+    # AIC: S = Q @ K^T  (f16 cube inputs, f32 L0C).
+    q_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((D // 16, BM // 16, 16, 16), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    k_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((BN // 16, D // 16, 16, 16), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    s_l0c = tla.alloc_buffer((BN // 16, BM // 16, 16, 16), tl.float32, space="l0c")
+    s_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((BM, BN), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    q_blk = tla.view(Q_ptr, (BM, D), strides=(D, 1))
+    k_blk = tla.view(K_ptr, (D, BN), strides=(1, D))  # K^T: column-major view of K
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        tla.copy(q_blk, q_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.copy(k_blk, k_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.cube.mmad(q_l1, k_l1, s_l0c, clear_accum=True)  # hivm.hir.mmadL1
+        tla.copy(s_l0c, s_ub)  # hivm.hir.fixpipe (NZ -> ND into UB)
+        # AIC: signal the softmax handoff only after fixpipe has written S.
+        tla.sync.block_set_flag(0, "FIX", FLAG_S)
+
+    # AIV: row-wise softmax of S in place (each row = one 64-lane f32 reg).
+    p_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((BM, BN), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    p_blk = tla.view(P_ptr, (BM, BN), strides=(BN, 1))
+    with tla.scope.vector():
+        # AIV: wait for S, then softmax each row and store P (f32) to GM.
+        tla.sync.block_wait_flag("V", FLAG_S)
+        with tla.scope.simd():
+            one = tla.simd.vfull(1.0, tl.float32, 64)
+            sc = tla.simd.vfull(SCALE, tl.float32, 64)
+            for r in tl.range(BM):
+                v = tla.simd.vmul(tla.simd.vlds(s_ub[r, 0]), sc)
+                m = tla.simd.vreduce_max(v)  # row max, broadcast
+                v = tla.simd.vadd(v, tla.simd.vneg(m))
+                e = tla.simd.vexp(v)  # ave.hir.vexp
+                l = tla.simd.vbroadcast(tla.simd.vreduce_sum(e), low=True)  # row sum
+                p = tla.simd.vmul(e, tla.simd.vdiv(one, l))
+                tla.simd.vsts(p_ub[r, 0], p)
+        tla.copy(p_ub, p_blk)  # hivm.hir.store (MTE3 UB->GM)
+        # AIV: signal the P round-trip only after the MTE3 store landed.
+        tla.sync.block_set_flag(0, "MTE3", FLAG_P)
+
+    # AIC: O = P @ V (f32 inputs -> f32 L0C).
+    p_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((BN // 16, BM // 16, 16, 16), tl.float32, space="l1")
+    v_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((N // 16, BN // 16, 16, 16), tl.float32, space="l1")
+    o_l0c = tla.alloc_buffer((N // 16, BM // 16, 16, 16), tl.float32, space="l0c")
+    o_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((BM, N), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    v_blk = tla.view(V_ptr, (BN, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    o_blk = tla.view(O_ptr, (BM, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        # AIC: wait for P, then load it back into L1 and accumulate O.
+        tla.sync.block_wait_flag("MTE2", FLAG_P)
+        tla.copy(p_blk, p_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.copy(v_blk, v_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.cube.mmad(p_l1, v_l1, o_l0c, clear_accum=True)  # hivm.hir.mmadL1
+        tla.copy(o_l0c, o_ub)  # hivm.hir.fixpipe (NZ -> ND into UB)
+        # AIC: signal the O handoff only after fixpipe has written O.
+        tla.sync.block_set_flag(0, "FIX", FLAG_O)
+
+    with tla.scope.vector():
+        # AIV: wait for O before the final UB->GM store.
+        tla.sync.block_wait_flag("MTE3", FLAG_O)
+        tla.copy(o_ub, o_blk)  # hivm.hir.store (MTE3 UB->GM)
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    s = SHAPE
+    return {
+        "BM": s["BM"], "BN": s["BN"], "D": s["D"], "N": s["N"], "SCALE": 1.0 / s["D"]**0.5, "FLAG_S": s["FLAG_S"],
+        "FLAG_P": s["FLAG_P"], "FLAG_O": s["FLAG_O"]
+    }
+
+
+# ---- torch reference (same semantics/shape) ----
+
+
+def _ref_torch(Q, K, V):
+    """Host reference: O = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(D)) @ V."""
+    s = SHAPE
+    p = torch.softmax(Q.float() @ K.float().T * (1.0 / s["D"]**0.5), dim=-1)  # (BM, BN)
+    return p @ V  # (BM, N)
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(flash_attn, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert "!tt.ptr" in text, "route A entry must keep pointer args at AST stage"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.pointer_cast") == 5, "tla.view(ptr) x5"
+    assert text.count("memref.reinterpret_cast") == 5, "tla.view(ptr) x5"
+    module = lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    check_lowered_ir(
+        text, loads=0, stores=2, buffers=9, extra=("#hivm.address_space<cbuf>", "#hivm.address_space<cc>",
+                                                   "#hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>", "#hivm.func_core_type<AIV>"))
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.nd2nz") == 4, "GM->L1 x4 (q, k, p, v)"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.mmadL1") == 2, "two gemms: S and O"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.fixpipe") == 2, "L0C->UB x2 (S, O)"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.sync_block_set") == 3, "AIC/AIV signals x3"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.sync_block_wait") == 3, "AIV/AIC waits x3"
+    assert text.count("ave.hir.vexp") == 1, "one exp inside the softmax row loop"
+    assert text.count("ave.hir.vload") == 1, "one row load inside the softmax row loop"
+
+    # Each handoff flag must follow its producer and precede its consumer.
+    def nth(pat, k):
+        """0-based index of the k-th occurrence (k is 1-based)."""
+        pos = -1
+        for _ in range(k):
+            pos = text.index(pat, pos + 1)
+        return pos
+
+    assert text.index("hivm.hir.fixpipe") < text.index("hivm.hir.sync_block_set"), "S flag after fixpipe"
+    assert text.index("hivm.hir.sync_block_wait") < text.index("ave.hir.vload"), "softmax waits for S"
+    assert nth("hivm.hir.sync_block_set", 2) > nth("hivm.hir.store", 1), "P flag after the P store"
+    assert nth("hivm.hir.sync_block_wait", 2) < nth("hivm.hir.nd2nz", 3), "AIC waits before reloading P"
+    assert nth("hivm.hir.sync_block_wait", 3) < nth("hivm.hir.store", 2), "O wait before the O store"
+    assert 'mix_mode = "mix"' in text, "cube+vector kernel must be tagged mix"
+    assert text.count("hivm.vector_function") == 1, "only the softmax SIMD scope is a VF"
+    print("IR PASS: flash_attn HIVM structure ok"
+          " (4 nd2nz / 2 mmadL1 / 2 fixpipe / 3 sync set+wait / 2 stores / 1 vexp in row loop)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    s = SHAPE
+    Q = torch.randn(s["BM"], s["D"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: device_print (route A: hivm.hir.debug directly).
+
+Semantics: copy GM->UB, print two UB slices outside the SIMD scope, then copy
+UB->GM inside it.  Each value emits one hivm.hir.debug op; buf[i0, i1, ...]
+element ranges lower to a 0-d memref subview so only that element is dumped.
+
+Validation (see device_print.py): calls inside a tla.scope and non-UB values
+(L1/GM) are rejected with RuntimeError.
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline-compile, assert hivm.hir.debug at AST stage and unchanged
+            after lower (the npuir chain auto-inserts init/finish_debug and
+            lowers the op to _mlir_ciface_print_* libcalls)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist
+  run     : real-device launch (prints go to the device debug tunnel)
+"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))  # tla_ut/
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+from triton.compiler.errors import CompilationError
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+SHAPE = dict(M=8, N=64)
+
+# offline compile signature (pointer entry takes pointer args).
+SIGNATURE = {"A_ptr": "*fp32"}
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def device_print_kernel(A_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
+    a_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    a_blk = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    tla.copy(a_blk, a_ub)  # GM -> UB (hivm.hir.load)
+    tla.device_print("ub[0, 0] = ", a_ub[0, 0])
+    tla.device_print("ub[0, 1] = ", a_ub[0, 1], hex=True)
+    with tla.scope.simd():
+        tla.copy(a_ub, a_blk)  # UB -> GM (hivm.hir.store)
+
+
+# negative kernels: must raise RuntimeError at compile time.
+def _bad_inside_scope():
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def k(A_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
+        a_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="ub")
+        a_blk = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+        tla.copy(a_blk, a_ub)
+        with tla.scope.simd():
+            tla.device_print("x = ", a_ub[0, 0])
+        tla.copy(a_ub, a_blk)
+
+    return k
+
+
+def _bad_l1():
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def k(A_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
+        a_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="l1")
+        a_blk = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+        tla.copy(a_blk, a_l1)
+        tla.device_print("x = ", a_l1[0, 0])
+        tla.copy(a_l1, a_blk)
+
+    return k
+
+
+def _bad_gm():
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def k(A_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
+        a_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="ub")
+        a_blk = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+        tla.copy(a_blk, a_ub)
+        tla.device_print("x = ", a_blk[0, 0])  # GM value
+        with tla.scope.simd():
+            tla.copy(a_ub, a_blk)
+
+    return k
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    s = SHAPE
+    return {"M": s["M"], "N": s["N"]}
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(device_print_kernel, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.debug") == 2, "device_print emits hivm.hir.debug at AST stage"
+    assert text.count("tt.print") == 0, "no tt.print on the TLA device_print path"
+    module = lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    for forbidden in ("!tt.ptr", "tt.ptr_to_int", "tensor<", "triton_print"):
+        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.debug") == 2, "hivm.hir.debug survives lower unchanged"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.load") == 1 and text.count("hivm.hir.store") == 1
+    # validation: inside-scope, L1, and GM prints must be rejected.  The
+    # frontend raises RuntimeError which ast_to_ttir wraps in CompilationError.
+    for bad in (_bad_inside_scope, _bad_l1, _bad_gm):
+        try:
+            compile_offline(bad(), SIGNATURE, constexprs())
+        except (RuntimeError, CompilationError) as e:
+            assert "tla.device_print" in str(e), f"unexpected rejection: {e}"
+        else:
+            raise AssertionError(f"expected RuntimeError from {bad.__name__}")
+    print("IR PASS: device_print (hivm.hir.debug x2, 1 load / 1 store, validation ok)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    s = SHAPE
+    A = torch.randn(s["M"], s["N"], dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    device_print_kernel[(1, )](A, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return A
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    _launch()
+    artifacts = check_compile_artifacts()
+    assert artifacts, "no .o/.npubin artifact in TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
+    print("COMPILE PASS: device_print generated artifacts", len(artifacts), "->", artifacts[0])
+
+
+def test_run():
+    _launch()
+    print("DEVICE_PRINT OK")
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: device_print", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: inter-core synchronization (cube -> vector handoff).
+
+Real kernel, modelled on ``cube/gemm_bias.py`` (tilelang ascend gemm + vector
+elementwise):
+
+    C = A @ B                       (cube: nd2nz x2 -> mmadL1 -> fixpipe to GM)
+    cube --block_set_flag--> flag 0 (raised only after C is in GM)
+    vector --block_wait_flag--> GM -> UB, O = C + bias over every 64-lane tile
+    vector -> O (GM)
+
+The flag protects the real inter-core dependency: the vector stage must not
+read C before the cube's fixpipe has written it to GM.
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline HIVM/AVE IR structure (no NPU, no torch)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist
+  run     : real-device launch + accuracy (SYNC_INTER OK)
+"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+M, N, K = 64, 64, 64
+BIAS = 1.0
+FLAG = 0
+
+SIGNATURE = {"A_ptr": "*fp16", "B_ptr": "*fp16", "C_ptr": "*fp32", "O_ptr": "*fp32"}
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def sync_inter(A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, O_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr, BIAS: tl.constexpr,
+               FLAG: tl.constexpr):
+    tl.static_assert(K % 16 == 0 and M % 16 == 0 and N % 16 == 0, "M/N/K must be multiples of 16 (cube tile)")
+    tl.static_assert((M * N) % 64 == 0, "M*N must be a multiple of 64")
+
+    a_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((M, K), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    b_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((K, N), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    c_l0c = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="l0c")
+    c_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="ub")
+
+    a = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, K), strides=(K, 1))
+    b = tla.view(B_ptr, (K, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    c = tla.view(C_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    o = tla.view(O_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        tla.copy(a, a_l1)
+        tla.copy(b, b_l1)
+        tla.cube.mmad(a_l1, b_l1, c_l0c, clear_accum=True)
+        tla.copy(c_l0c, c)
+        # Raise the flag only after fixpipe has written C to GM.
+        tla.sync.block_set_flag(0, "FIX", FLAG)
+
+    # Vector side: wait for the cube result, then post-process the whole tile.
+    tla.sync.block_wait_flag("MTE2", FLAG)
+    tla.copy(c, c_ub)
+    with tla.scope.simd():
+        bias = tla.simd.vfull(BIAS, tl.float32, 64)
+        for i in tl.static_range((M * N) // 64):
+            row = i // (N // 64)
+            col = (i % (N // 64)) * 64
+            v = tla.simd.vlds(c_ub[row, col], dist="NORM")
+            tla.simd.vsts(c_ub[row, col], tla.simd.vadd(v, bias), dist="NORM_B32")
+    tla.copy(c_ub, o)
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    return {"M": M, "N": N, "K": K, "BIAS": BIAS, "FLAG": FLAG}
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(sync_inter, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir))
+    check_lowered_ir(text, loads=1, stores=1, buffers=4, extra=("#hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>", 'mix_mode = "mix"'))
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.nd2nz") == 2, text
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.mmadL1") == 1, text
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.fixpipe") == 1, text
+    assert text.count("ave.hir.vadd") == (M * N) // 64, text
+    set_line = next(l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if "hivm.hir.sync_block_set" in l)
+    wait_line = next(l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if "hivm.hir.sync_block_wait" in l)
+    assert set_line.startswith("hivm.hir.sync_block_set[<CUBE>, <PIPE_FIX>, <PIPE_FIX>] "
+                               f"flag = {FLAG}"), set_line
+    assert wait_line.startswith("hivm.hir.sync_block_wait[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_MTE2>, <PIPE_MTE2>] "
+                                f"flag = {FLAG}"), wait_line
+    for line in (set_line, wait_line):
+        assert "sync_instr_mode = <INTER_BLOCK_SYNCHRONIZATION>" in line, line
+    assert text.index("fixpipe") < text.index("sync_block_set"), \
+        "the flag must follow the GM write"
+    assert text.index("sync_block_wait") < text.index("hivm.hir.load"), \
+        "the vector load must wait for the flag"
+    print("IR PASS: sync_inter (gemm -> fixpipe -> flag -> vector bias -> O)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    import torch
+    A = torch.randn(M, K, dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(K, N, dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    C = torch.zeros(M, N, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    O = torch.full((M, N), -7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    sync_inter[(1, )](A, B, C, O, enable_tla_mode=True, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return A, B, C, O
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    _launch()
+    artifacts = check_compile_artifacts()
+    assert artifacts, "no .o/.npubin artifact in TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
+    print("COMPILE PASS: sync_inter")
+
+
+def test_run():
+    import numpy as np
+    A, B, C, O = _launch()
+    ref_c = (A.float() @ B.float()).cpu().numpy()
+    got_c = C.cpu().numpy()
+    got_o = O.cpu().numpy()
+    ok_c = np.allclose(got_c, ref_c, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+    ok_o = np.allclose(got_o, ref_c + np.float32(BIAS), atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+    print("SYNC_INTER_GEMM", "OK" if ok_c else "MISMATCH")
+    print("SYNC_INTER_BIAS", "OK" if ok_o else "MISMATCH")
+    assert ok_c and ok_o, "sync_inter accuracy mismatch"
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: sync_inter", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: intra-core synchronization.
+
+Real kernel: ``out = a + b`` on f32 with the pipeline fully hand-synchronized:
+
+    GM -> UB (MTE2)  --set/wait_flag-->  vector add (V)  --barrier-->
+    UB -> GM (MTE3)  --sync_all-->  next AIV block
+
+The sync calls are inserted manually between the DMA and vector stages, so
+the test verifies both that the emitted synchronization is correct and that a
+real dependency chain still produces the right values.
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline HIVM/AVE IR structure (no NPU, no torch)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist
+  run     : real-device launch + accuracy (SYNC_INTRA OK)
+"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+N = 64  # f32 vector-register lane count (2048 bits)
+
+SIGNATURE = {"A_ptr": "*fp32", "B_ptr": "*fp32", "O_ptr": "*fp32"}
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def sync_intra(A_ptr, B_ptr, O_ptr, N: tl.constexpr):
+    a_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((N, ), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    b_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((N, ), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    o_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((N, ), tl.float32, space="ub")
+    a = tla.view(A_ptr, (N, ), strides=(1, ), offsets=(0, ))
+    b = tla.view(B_ptr, (N, ), strides=(1, ), offsets=(0, ))
+    o = tla.view(O_ptr, (N, ), strides=(1, ), offsets=(0, ))
+
+    tla.copy(a, a_ub)
+    tla.copy(b, b_ub)
+    # GM -> UB must finish before the vector stage reads the buffers.
+    tla.sync.set_flag("MTE2", "V", 0)
+    tla.sync.wait_flag("MTE2", "V", 0)
+
+    with tla.scope.simd():
+        av = tla.simd.vlds(a_ub[0], dist="NORM")
+        bv = tla.simd.vlds(b_ub[0], dist="NORM")
+        tla.simd.vsts(o_ub[0], tla.simd.vadd(av, bv), dist="NORM_B32")
+
+    # Vector register writes must be visible before the UB -> GM store.
+    tla.sync.barrier("ALL")
+    tla.sync.set_flag("V", "MTE3", 1)
+    tla.sync.wait_flag("V", "MTE3", 1)
+    tla.copy(o_ub, o)
+
+    # Hardware barrier across the AIV blocks after the GM writes.
+    tla.sync.sync_all(False)
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    return {"N": N}
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(sync_intra, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir))
+    check_lowered_ir(text, loads=2, stores=1, buffers=3)
+    for op in ("hivm.hir.set_flag", "hivm.hir.wait_flag", "hivm.hir.pipe_barrier", "hivm.hir.sync_block"):
+        assert text.count(op) == (2 if "flag" in op else 1), text
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.set_flag[<PIPE_MTE2>, <PIPE_V>") == 1, text
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.wait_flag[<PIPE_MTE2>, <PIPE_V>") == 1, text
+    assert "<EVENT_ID0>" in text and "<EVENT_ID1>" in text, text
+    assert "hivm.hir.set_flag[<PIPE_V>, <PIPE_MTE3>" in text, text
+    assert "hivm.hir.pipe_barrier[<PIPE_ALL>]" in text, text
+    assert "hivm.hir.sync_block[<ALL_VECTOR>]" in text, text
+    assert text.count("ave.hir.vadd") == 1, text
+    order = [
+        text.index(op)
+        for op in ("hivm.hir.set_flag", "hivm.hir.wait_flag", "ave.hir.vadd", "hivm.hir.pipe_barrier", "hivm.hir.store")
+    ]
+    assert order == sorted(order), "sync ops must stay between the stages"
+    print("IR PASS: sync_intra (MTE2->V->MTE3 hand sync, barrier, sync_all)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    import torch
+    A = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    O = torch.full((N, ), -7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    sync_intra[(1, )](A, B, O, enable_tla_mode=True, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return A, B, O
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    _launch()
+    artifacts = check_compile_artifacts()
+    assert artifacts, "no .o/.npubin artifact in TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
+    print("COMPILE PASS: sync_intra")
+
+
+def test_run():
+    import numpy as np
+    A, B, O = _launch()
+    ref = A.cpu().numpy() + B.cpu().numpy()
+    ok = np.allclose(O.cpu().numpy(), ref, atol=0.0, rtol=0.0)
+    print("SYNC_INTRA", "OK" if ok else "MISMATCH")
+    assert ok, "sync_intra accuracy mismatch"
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: sync_intra", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+// RUN: triton-opt --add-control-flow-condition %s | FileCheck %s
+
+// VECTOR and CUBE each have one main scf.for and one intraDeps pair, so the
+// pipeline reaches SplittedIfWrapSsbufIf. The two pairs use different intra
+// groups: one group lists every producer, and calculateFactor looks those
+// producers up inside the current for. Block 5's mulf is inside one
+// splitted_if. The new if's else adds the block counter and the for step.
+// ProcessArgs appends one shared iter_arg, then UpdateLoopOps appends block
+// counters. The first counter is the third iter_arg, initialized to the for
+// lower bound.
+
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @wrap_for_splitted_if
+// CHECK: scf.for %{{[^ ]+}} = %[[LB:[^ ]+]] to %{{[^ ]+}} step %[[STEP:[^ ]+]] iter_args(%{{[^ ]+}} = %{{[^ ]+}}, %{{[^ ]+}} = %{{[^ ]+}}, %[[CTR:[^ ]+]] = %[[LB]]
+// CHECK: %[[SPLIT:[^ ]+]] = arith.cmpi sgt, {{.*}}ssbuffer.block_id = 5 : i32
+// CHECK: scf.if %[[SPLIT]]
+// CHECK: arith.mulf {{.*}} : tensor<4xf32>
+// CHECK: } {{.*}}ssbuffer.if = 5 : i32}
+// CHECK: arith.addi %[[CTR]], %[[STEP]]
+// CHECK: } {{.*}}ssbuffer.splitted_if = 0 : i32}
+
+module attributes {hacc.target = #hacc.target<"Ascend950PR_9579">, ssbuffer.intra_buf_count = 2 : i32} {
+  func.func @wrap_for_splitted_if() attributes {global_kernel = "local", mix_mode = "mix", parallel_mode = "simd"} {
+    %c0_i32 = arith.constant 0 : i32
+    %c1_i32 = arith.constant 1 : i32
+    %c16_i32 = arith.constant 16 : i32
+    %zero = arith.constant dense<0.000000e+00> : tensor<4xf32>
+    %one = arith.constant dense<1.000000e+00> : tensor<4xf32>
+
+    scope.scope : () -> () {
+      %0 = scf.for %arg0 = %c0_i32 to %c16_i32 step %c1_i32
+          iter_args(%arg1 = %c0_i32) -> (i32) : i32 {
+        %split = arith.cmpi sgt, %arg0, %c0_i32 {ssbuffer.block_id = 5 : i32} : i32
+        scf.if %split {
+          %t = arith.mulf %zero, %one : tensor<4xf32>
+        } {ssbuffer.block_id = 5 : i32, ssbuffer.splitted_if = 0 : i32}
+        %prod = arith.addi %arg1, %c0_i32 {ssbuffer.block_id = 5 : i32, ssbuffer.intraDeps = [0 : i32, 1 : i32]} : i32
+        %cons = arith.addi %arg1, %c1_i32 {ssbuffer.block_id = 7 : i32, ssbuffer.intraDeps = [0 : i32, 0 : i32]} : i32
+        scf.yield %cons : i32
+      } {ssbuffer.main_loop = 0 : i32}
+      scope.return
+    } {hivm.tcore_type = #hivm.tcore_type<VECTOR>}
+
+    scope.scope : () -> () {
+      %0 = scf.for %arg0 = %c0_i32 to %c16_i32 step %c1_i32
+          iter_args(%arg1 = %c0_i32) -> (i32) : i32 {
+        %prod = arith.addi %arg1, %c0_i32 {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.intraDeps = [1 : i32, 1 : i32]} : i32
+        %cons = arith.addi %arg1, %c1_i32 {ssbuffer.block_id = 3 : i32, ssbuffer.intraDeps = [1 : i32, 0 : i32]} : i32
+        scf.yield %cons : i32
+      } {ssbuffer.main_loop = 0 : i32}
+      scope.return
+    } {hivm.tcore_type = #hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>}
