commits.message:
[ascend](feat) bug fix and refactor for TLA frontend (#2744)

* [TritonToLinalg](fix) keep source memory space in pointer_cast rewrite

finalizePointerCasts now builds the pointer_cast result memref from the
source memory space of the cast type instead of dropping it. A TLA GM
pointer entry on a 1-D pointer_cast must survive the rewrite, otherwise
the downstream memref.reinterpret_cast compares a plain memref<?xf32>
against a GM result type and fails verification. Add a lit test under
tla_ut/mlir asserting the space-preserving rewrite for GM pointer
entries.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](refactor) extract AscendNPUIROpBuilder

Extract the shared AscendNPUIROpBuilder base out of ascend_ir.cc into
include/Utils/AscendNPUIROpBuilder.h so backend-local subclasses can
inherit it across TUs, while pybind registration stays module_local to
the ascend plugin module. Remove the inline OpBuilder definition from
ascend_ir.cc in favor of the shared header, and introduce tla_builder.cc
with the full TLABuilder bindings (AVE SIMD/VF ops, TLA buffer helpers,
hivm load/store and scope ops), wired into the ascend "ir" submodule via
triton_ascend.cc.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add TLA cube scope, mmad and DMA copy routes

Implement the tilelang-ascend-style cube path on top of the TLA
frontend: scope.cube outlines to a real AIC scope
(#hivm.func_core_type<AIC>, no vector_mode) whose body carries
tla.cube.mmad (hivm.hir.mmadL1) and tla.copy routes for GM->L1
(hivm.hir.nd2nz), L0C->UB/GM (hivm.hir.fixpipe, dma_mode inferred
from dst rank: 2D -> nz2nd, 4D -> normal).

C++ side (tla_builder.cc) binds create_hivm_nd2nz/fixpipe/mmadl1 and
reworks create_scope_op to return the OpState alone plus a new
get_scope_entry_block exposed with py::return_value_policy::reference.
This fixes a pybind ownership bug: Block is wrapped without a
py::nodelete holder, so the previous std::pair<OpState, Block*> return
let the automatic policy delete the scope region block when the Python
wrapper was GC'd, emptying the scope region and corrupting the block
list. ast_to_ttir now mirrors the runtime Ascend patch and injects
TargetDevice enum symbol, e.g. Ascend910_9589, since
symbolizeTargetDeviceEnum matches exactly) so FixpipeOp::verify
accepts dst=UB / NZ2DN fixpipe on Ascend950.

Kernel mode now has a single TLA-side entry: _infer_kernel_mode tags
the ttadapter entry mix_mode="mix" when the module carries cube work
(hivm.hir.mmadL1, the marker the scope-level AIC tagging in
code_generator._vf_scope_attrs is built on), instead of letting
TritonToLinalgPass tag TLA cube kernels "aiv" (it only sees TTIR dot /
hivm CustomOps). A new tla_builder set_op_attr binding writes the attr
on the entry operation directly, because module.get_function misses it
after triton_to_linalg lowers the entry from triton::FuncOp to mlir
func::FuncOp.

Two offline TLA tests under unittest/tla_ut/cube (gemm_basic,
gemm_bias) lock the generated ttadapter-boundary IR: scope attrs,
nd2nz/mmadL1/fixpipe/store counts, buffer address spaces, the
kernel-entry ABI attributes and the mix_mode tag; the vector regression
(norm_forward) stays green.

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add tla.reshape rank-only buffer reshape frontend

Add a tla.reshape builtin that reinterprets a contiguous row-major buffer
under a new static shape, lowering to memref.collapse_shape/expand_shape
with explicit reassociation indices (mirroring npuir's
CanonicalizeTensorReshape): flatten to 1-D when the source rank is > 1,
then unflatten to the target shape when its rank is > 1, so pure
flatten/unflatten emit a single op.  Element counts must match and the
source must be an identity-layout buffer; strided tiles and count
mismatches are rejected at trace time.  Expose the two reshape ops on the
TLA builder (create_tla_collapse_shape/create_tla_expand_shape, factored
into a shared template) and add an offline IR test covering flatten,
unflatten, merge+split and split cases plus the two negative paths.

* [extension](refactor) per-class TLA scope attrs, drop VF effect recording

Motivation: AIC (cube) scopes must not carry hivm.vector_function or the
outline marker, otherwise outline-scope extracts them into an AIV vector
function; the tla.memory_effect attribute and its _VF_EFFECTS inference
are unused.

Design: each scope class (simd/cube) owns mlir_attrs(builder), so adding
a new scope type only needs a subclass; SIMD scopes keep the manual-VF
markers, cube scopes carry only hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>. The
tla.memory_effect attribute, the dummy-visit effect inference and the
simd._record_vf_effect plumbing are removed. The vf module is renamed to
scope.py to match the tla.scope namespace.

Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) add pytest one-click runner for tla_ut cases

Motivation: tla_ut case files are named by op (rope.py, cast_back.py, ...)
and driven by env TLA_TEST_STAGE through a per-file main(); pytest's default
test_*.py pattern collects none of them, and the root unittest/conftest.py
assign_npu fixture crashes on machines without an NPU, so the 3-in-1
ir/compile/run cases could only run one file at a time. A pytest.ini-based
collection also collides with the repo .gitignore.

Design: tla_ut/conftest.py collects every *.py module via pytest_collect_file
(except conftest.py itself), maps TLA_TEST_STAGE onto pytest skips via
utils.tla_test_utils.get_stages(), shadows the root assign_npu fixture for
no-NPU ir-only mode, and supplies the output_dir fixture used by
test_ir(output_dir=None). Any tla_ut subdirectory can be run directly with
pytest, including pytest . at the unittest root. The per-case
python <case>.py entry keeps working unchanged.

Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

* [ascend](feat) isolate TLA SIMD register values from Triton tensors

Motivation: TLA SIMD ops were front-end wrapped as tl.tensor, letting Triton
block semantics leak into SIMD register values. Vector values will also be
carried across scf.for iterations, which requires a dedicated value type with
the same __eq__/mangle protocol as buffer_type.
Design: add tla.vector/tla.vector_type wrapping MLIR vector<NxT> handles, with
to_ir/mangle/__eq__ and flatten protocols mirroring tla.buffer/buffer_type;
bind create_tla_vector_type in tla_builder.cc. Switch SIMD results and
predicates to tla.vector, validate operands/masks, keep scalar tensor indices,
and factor the duplicated binary/interleave bodies into _binary/_interleave.
SIMD ops are written directly inside tla.scope.simd() (ave.hir ops cannot be
inlined through tt.call helpers).
Risks: None

Assisted-by: AI

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: gemm_basic (TLA direct port of tilelang ascend gemm).
+
+Semantics: C[M, N] = A[M, K] @ B[K, N]  (fp16 in, f32 accumulate in L0C)
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline-compile the HIVM IR handed to npuir and assert
+            (2 nd2nz / 1 mmadL1 / 1 fixpipe, cbuf/cc alloc, cube scope
+            carries only hivm.tcore_type<CUBE> and is not a VF)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist
+  run     : real-device launch + accuracy (GEMM_BASIC OK; standard Triton
+            reference gemm_triton, same semantics/shape -> TRITON_GEMM_BASIC OK)
+
+v1 scope: single block (M=N=K=64), clear_accum=True one-shot; no K-loop
+pipelining / multi-core.
+"""
+import sys, os
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))  # tests/
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+# default shapes: M, N, K (K must be a multiple of 16)
+SHAPE = dict(M=64, N=64, K=64)
+
+# offline compile signature (pointer entry takes pointer args).
+SIGNATURE = {"A_ptr": "*fp16", "B_ptr": "*fp16", "C_ptr": "*fp32"}
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def gemm_basic(A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr):
+    tl.static_assert(K % 16 == 0 and M % 16 == 0 and N % 16 == 0, "M/N/K must be multiples of 16 (cube tile)")
+    a_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((M, K), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    b_l1 = tla.alloc_buffer((K, N), tl.float16, space="l1")
+    c_l0c = tla.alloc_buffer((M, N), tl.float32, space="l0c")
+    a_blk = tla.view(A_ptr, (M, K), strides=(K, 1))
+    b_blk = tla.view(B_ptr, (K, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    c_blk = tla.view(C_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        tla.copy(a_blk, a_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.copy(b_blk, b_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.cube.mmad(a_l1, b_l1, c_l0c, clear_accum=True)  # hivm.hir.mmadL1
+        tla.copy(c_l0c, c_blk)  # hivm.hir.fixpipe (2D dst -> nz2nd)
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    s = SHAPE
+    return {"M": s["M"], "N": s["N"], "K": s["K"]}
+
+
+# ---- standard Triton reference (same semantics/shape) ----
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def gemm_triton(A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr):
+    rows = tl.arange(0, M)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, N)
+    a = tl.load(A_ptr + rows[:, None] * K + cols[None, :])  # (M, K)
+    b = tl.load(B_ptr + cols[:, None] * K + rows[None, :])  # (N, K) -> load B(K, N) transposed
+    c = tl.sum(a[:, :, None] * b[None, :, :], axis=1)  # (M, N) f32 accumulate
+    tl.store(C_ptr + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], c)
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(gemm_basic, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert "!tt.ptr" in text, "route A entry must keep pointer args at AST stage"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.pointer_cast") == 3, "tla.view(ptr) x3"
+    assert text.count("memref.reinterpret_cast") == 3, "tla.view(ptr) x3"
+    module = lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    check_lowered_ir(text, loads=0, stores=0, buffers=3,
+                     extra=("#hivm.address_space<cbuf>", "#hivm.address_space<cc>", "#hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>"))
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.nd2nz") == 2, "GM->L1 x2"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.mmadL1") == 1, "one gemm"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.fixpipe") == 1, "L0C->GM"
+    assert 'mix_mode = "mix"' in text, "kernel with cube work must be tagged mix"
+    # Pure-cube kernel: AIC scope is not a vector function, so no VF markers
+    # (hivm.vector_function / func_core_type / outline) may appear.
+    assert text.count("hivm.vector_function") == 0, "cube scope must not be a VF"
+    assert "hivm.memory_effect" not in text, "VF effect recording was removed"
+    print("IR PASS: gemm_basic HIVM structure ok (2 nd2nz / 1 mmadL1 / 1 fixpipe)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    s = SHAPE
+    A = torch.randn(s["M"], s["K"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(s["K"], s["N"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    C = torch.full((s["M"], s["N"]), 7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    gemm_basic[(1, )](A, B, C, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return C, (A.float() @ B.float())
+
+
+def _launch_triton():
+    s = SHAPE
+    A = torch.randn(s["M"], s["K"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(s["K"], s["N"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    C = torch.full((s["M"], s["N"]), 7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    gemm_triton[(1, )](A, B, C, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return C, (A.float() @ B.float())
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    _launch()
+    artifacts = check_compile_artifacts()
+    assert artifacts, "no .o/.npubin artifact in TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
+    print("COMPILE PASS: gemm_basic generated artifacts", len(artifacts), "->", artifacts[0])
+
+
+def test_run():
+    C, ref = _launch()
+    oc, rc = C.cpu(), ref.cpu()
+    print("C[:4,:4]  :", oc[:4, :4].tolist())
+    print("ref[:4,:4]:", rc[:4, :4].tolist())
+    ok = torch.allclose(oc, rc, atol=0.05)
+    print("GEMM_BASIC", "OK" if ok else "MISMATCH", "M", SHAPE["M"], "N", SHAPE["N"], "K", SHAPE["K"])
+    assert ok, "gemm_basic e2e mismatch"
+    # standard Triton reference.
+    Ct, rt = _launch_triton()
+    oc_t, rc_t = Ct.cpu(), rt.cpu()
+    bad_t = ((oc_t - rc_t).abs() > 0.05).nonzero().flatten()
+    print("TRITON_GEMM_BASIC", "OK" if bad_t.numel() == 0 else "MISMATCH", "num_mismatch:", bad_t.numel())
+    assert bad_t.numel() == 0, "standard triton gemm_triton mismatch"
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: gemm_basic", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+    c_blk = tla.view(C_ptr, (M, N), strides=(N, 1))
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        tla.copy(a_blk, a_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.copy(b_blk, b_l1)  # hivm.hir.nd2nz
+        tla.cube.mmad(a_l1, b_l1, c_l0c, clear_accum=True)  # hivm.hir.mmadL1
+        tla.copy(c_l0c, c_ub)  # hivm.hir.fixpipe (2D ub dst -> nz2nd, ND into UB)
+    with tla.scope.simd():
+        bias = tla.simd.vfull(BIAS, tl.float32, 64)
+        for i in tl.static_range((M * N) // 64):
+            row = i // (N // 64)
+            col = (i % (N // 64)) * 64
+            v = tla.simd.vlds(c_ub[row, col])  # NORM, ND row-major read
+            tla.simd.vsts(c_ub[row, col], tla.simd.vadd(v, bias))
+    tla.copy(c_ub, c_blk)  # hivm.hir.store (MTE3 UB->GM)
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    s = SHAPE
+    return {"M": s["M"], "N": s["N"], "K": s["K"], "BIAS": s["BIAS"]}
+
+
+# ---- standard Triton reference (same semantics/shape) ----
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def gemm_bias_triton(A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, M: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr, BIAS: tl.constexpr):
+    rows = tl.arange(0, M)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, N)
+    a = tl.load(A_ptr + rows[:, None] * K + cols[None, :])
+    b = tl.load(B_ptr + cols[:, None] * K + rows[None, :])
+    c = tl.sum(a[:, :, None] * b[None, :, :], axis=1) + BIAS
+    tl.store(C_ptr + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], c)
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(gemm_bias, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert "!tt.ptr" in text, "route A entry must keep pointer args at AST stage"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.pointer_cast") == 3, "tla.view(ptr) x3"
+    assert text.count("memref.reinterpret_cast") == 3, "tla.view(ptr) x3"
+    module = lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    check_lowered_ir(
+        text, loads=0, stores=1, buffers=4, extra=("#hivm.address_space<cbuf>", "#hivm.address_space<cc>",
+                                                   "#hivm.tcore_type<CUBE>", "#hivm.func_core_type<AIV>"))
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.nd2nz") == 2, "GM->L1 x2"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.mmadL1") == 1, "one gemm"
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.fixpipe") == 1, "L0C->UB"
+    assert 'mix_mode = "mix"' in text, "cube+vector kernel must be tagged mix"
+    # The AIC (cube) scope is not a vector function: hivm.vector_function may
+    # appear only on the SIMD scope (exactly once), and the tla.memory_effect
+    # attribute was dropped with the VF effect recording.
+    assert text.count("hivm.vector_function") == 1, "only the SIMD scope is a VF"
+    assert "hivm.memory_effect" not in text, "VF effect recording was removed"
+    print("IR PASS: gemm_bias HIVM structure ok (2 nd2nz / 1 mmadL1 / 1 fixpipe / 1 store)")
+
+
+def _launch():
+    s = SHAPE
+    A = torch.randn(s["M"], s["K"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(s["K"], s["N"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    C = torch.full((s["M"], s["N"]), 7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    gemm_bias[(1, )](A, B, C, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return C, (A.float() @ B.float() + s["BIAS"])
+
+
+def _launch_triton():
+    s = SHAPE
+    A = torch.randn(s["M"], s["K"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    B = torch.randn(s["K"], s["N"], dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    C = torch.full((s["M"], s["N"]), 7.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    gemm_bias_triton[(1, )](A, B, C, **constexprs())
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return C, (A.float() @ B.float() + s["BIAS"])
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    _launch()
+    artifacts = check_compile_artifacts()
+    assert artifacts, "no .o/.npubin artifact in TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
+    print("COMPILE PASS: gemm_bias generated artifacts", len(artifacts), "->", artifacts[0])
+
+
+def test_run():
+    C, ref = _launch()
+    oc, rc = C.cpu(), ref.cpu()
+    print("C[:4,:4]  :", oc[:4, :4].tolist())
+    print("ref[:4,:4]:", rc[:4, :4].tolist())
+    ok = torch.allclose(oc, rc, atol=0.05)
+    print("GEMM_BIAS", "OK" if ok else "MISMATCH", "M", SHAPE["M"], "N", SHAPE["N"], "K", SHAPE["K"])
+    assert ok, "gemm_bias e2e mismatch"
+    # standard Triton reference.
+    Ct, rt = _launch_triton()
+    oc_t, rc_t = Ct.cpu(), rt.cpu()
+    bad_t = ((oc_t - rc_t).abs() > 0.05).nonzero().flatten()
+    print("TRITON_GEMM_BIAS", "OK" if bad_t.numel() == 0 else "MISMATCH", "num_mismatch:", bad_t.numel())
+    assert bad_t.numel() == 0, "standard triton gemm_bias_triton mismatch"
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: gemm_bias", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+

+    main()

+"""TLA 3-in-1 test: buffer reshape (memref.reshape).
+
+Semantics: rank-only reinterpretation of a contiguous row-major buffer, element
+count preserved.  Covers flatten (2D->1D), unflatten (1D->2D), merge+split
+(2D->2D) and split (2D->3D); strided sources and element-count mismatches are
+rejected at trace time.
+
+Stages (env TLA_TEST_STAGE, default all with auto-degrade):
+  ir      : offline HIVM IR assert (2 collapse / 3 expand / 4 load / 4 store /
+            4 multibuffer / 6 pointer entries)
+  compile : full compile, confirm .o/.npubin artifacts exist (TODO: needs
+            npuir memref.reshape lowering)
+  run     : real-device launch + accuracy (TODO)
+"""
+import sys, os
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))  # tests/
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from triton.compiler.errors import CompilationError
+from utils.tla_test_utils import (get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_compile_artifacts)
+
+# H=4, D=8 -> 32 elements; every target shape below keeps the element count.
+SHAPE = dict(H=4, D=8)
+
+SIGNATURE = {"X_ptr": "*bf16", "O_ptr": "*bf16"}
+
+
+def constexprs():
+    return dict(SHAPE)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def reshape_fwd(X_ptr, O_ptr, H: tl.constexpr, D: tl.constexpr):
+    # Branches A/C/D share the same (H, D) GM tile; B reads the flat (H*D,) tile.
+    x_tile = tla.view(X_ptr, (H, D), strides=(D, 1), offsets=(0, 0))
+    x_flat = tla.view(X_ptr, (H * D, ), strides=(1, ), offsets=(0, ))
+
+    # A: (H, D) -> (H*D,)  flatten
+    ub_a = tla.alloc_buffer((H, D), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    tla.copy(x_tile, ub_a)
+    a = tla.reshape(ub_a, (H * D, ))
+    tla.copy(a, tla.view(O_ptr, (H * D, ), strides=(1, ), offsets=(0, )))
+
+    # B: (H*D,) -> (H, D)  unflatten
+    ub_b = tla.alloc_buffer((H * D, ), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    tla.copy(x_flat, ub_b)
+    b = tla.reshape(ub_b, (H, D))
+    tla.copy(b, tla.view(O_ptr, (H, D), strides=(D, 1), offsets=(0, 0)))
+
+    # C: (H, D) -> (H//2, 2*D)  split dim0 + merge dim1
+    ub_c = tla.alloc_buffer((H, D), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    tla.copy(x_tile, ub_c)
+    c = tla.reshape(ub_c, (H // 2, 2 * D))
+    tla.copy(c, tla.view(O_ptr, (H // 2, 2 * D), strides=(2 * D, 1), offsets=(0, 0)))
+
+    # D: (H, D) -> (H//2, 2, D)  split dim0 into two
+    ub_d = tla.alloc_buffer((H, D), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    tla.copy(x_tile, ub_d)
+    d = tla.reshape(ub_d, (H // 2, 2, D))
+    tla.copy(d, tla.view(O_ptr, (H // 2, 2, D), strides=(2 * D, D, 1), offsets=(0, 0, 0)))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def reshape_strided(X_ptr, O_ptr, H: tl.constexpr, D: tl.constexpr):
+    x_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((H, D), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    x = tla.view(X_ptr, (H, D), strides=(D, 1), offsets=(0, 0))
+    tla.copy(x, x_ub)
+    sub = tla.view(x_ub, (H, D // 2), strides=(1, 2), offsets=(0, 0))  # strided tile
+    tla.reshape(sub, (H * D // 2, ))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def reshape_count_mismatch(X_ptr, O_ptr, H: tl.constexpr, D: tl.constexpr):
+    x_ub = tla.alloc_buffer((H, D), tl.bfloat16, space="ub")
+    x = tla.view(X_ptr, (H, D), strides=(D, 1), offsets=(0, 0))
+    tla.copy(x, x_ub)
+    tla.reshape(x_ub, (H, 2 * D))  # 32 -> 64
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(reshape_fwd, SIGNATURE, constexprs(), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert "!tt.ptr" in text, "route A entry must keep pointer args at AST stage"
+    module = lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    check_lowered_ir(text, loads=4, stores=4, buffers=4)
+    assert text.count("memref.reshape") == 0, "reshape must decompose to expand/collapse"
+    # A (4,8)->(32,): pure collapse; B (32,)->(4,8): pure expand;
+    # C (4,8)->(2,16): collapse-to-1D then expand; D (4,8)->(2,2,8) is a pure
+    # expand (4 -> 2x2) so triton_to_linalg's canonicalizer folds its
+    # collapse+expand pair into a single expand.
+    assert text.count("memref.collapse_shape") == 2, "collapses: A, C"
+    assert text.count("memref.expand_shape") == 3, "expands: B, C, D"
+    # Result-type fingerprints pin each reshape to exactly one op: A/C collapse
+    # into 1-D, B expands back to (4,8), C to (2,16), D straight to (2,2,8).
+    assert text.count("into memref<32xbf16") == 2, "flatten results: A, C"
+    assert text.count("into memref<4x8xbf16") == 1, "unflatten result: B"
+    assert text.count("into memref<2x16xbf16") == 1, "merge+split result: C"
+    assert text.count("into memref<2x2x8xbf16") == 1, "split result: D"
+    # 2 shared in-tiles + 4 out views.
+    assert text.count("hivm.hir.pointer_cast") == 6, "tla.view(ptr) x6"
+    assert text.count("memref.reinterpret_cast") == 6, "tla.view(ptr) x6"
+    print("IR PASS: reshape HIVM structure ok (2 collapse / 3 expand / 4 load / 4 store / 4 multibuffer)")
+    # Negative cases: strided source and element-count mismatch must be
+    # rejected at trace time (the generator wraps the frontend ValueError in
+    # CompilationError, keeping the message).
+    rejects = {
+        reshape_strided: "contiguous row-major",
+        reshape_count_mismatch: "element count mismatch",
+    }
+    for fn, reason in rejects.items():
+        try:
+            compile_offline(fn, SIGNATURE, constexprs())
+            raise AssertionError(f"{fn.__name__} should raise ValueError")
+        except CompilationError as e:
+            assert reason in str(e), f"{fn.__name__} rejected for wrong reason: {e}"
+    print("NEG PASS: strided / count-mismatch reshape rejected")
+
+
+def test_compile():
+    raise NotImplementedError("reshape compile/run needs npuir memref.reshape lowering (TODO)")
+
+
+def test_run():
+    raise NotImplementedError("reshape compile/run needs npuir memref.reshape lowering (TODO)")
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    if do_ir:
+        test_ir()
+    if do_compile:
+        test_compile()
+    if do_run:
+        test_run()
+    print("ALL PASS: reshape", "ir" if do_ir else "", "compile" if do_compile else "", "run" if do_run else "")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+def test_type_protocol():

+    assert ty == tla.vector_type(64, tl.float32)
+    assert ty != tla.vector_type(128, tl.float32)
+    assert ty != tl.block_type(tl.float32, [64])
+    assert tla.vector_type(64, tl.int32) != tla.vector_type(64, tl.uint32)
+    assert tla.vector_type(64, tl.int32).mangle() != tla.vector_type(64, tl.uint32).mangle()
+    assert tla.vector_type(64, tl.int1).shape == (64, )
+    handle = object()
+    value, cursor = ty._unflatten_ir([None, handle], 1)
+    assert cursor == 2 and value.handle is handle
+    assert value.dtype == tl.float32 and value.shape == (64, )
+    assert not isinstance(value, tl.tensor)
+    handles = []
+    value._flatten_ir(handles)
+    assert handles == [handle]
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="scalar condition"):
+        bool(value)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lanes", [0, -1, True, 1.5])
+def test_invalid_lanes(lanes):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive compile-time integer"):
+        tla.vector_type(lanes, tl.float32)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [tl.pointer_type(tl.float32), tl.block_type(tl.float32, [64]), "fp32"])
+def test_invalid_element_type(dtype):
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="scalar integer or floating-point"):
+        tla.vector_type(64, dtype)
+
+
+class NoBuilder:
+    """Invalid inputs must fail before reaching any builder operation."""
+
+    @property
+    def builder(self):
+        raise AssertionError("invalid SIMD input reached the builder")
+
+
+def test_operand_validation():
+    sem = NoBuilder()
+    vec = tla.vector(None, tla.vector_type(64, tl.float32))
+    tensor = tl.tensor(None, tl.block_type(tl.float32, [64]))
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="tla.vector"):
+        tla.simd.vadd(tensor, tensor, _semantic=sem)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="same-typed"):
+        tla.simd.vadd(vec, tla.vector(None, tla.vector_type(128, tl.float32)), _semantic=sem)
+    for mask in (vec, tla.vector(None, tla.vector_type(128, tl.int1))):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mask must be"):
+            tla.simd.vsel(mask, vec, vec, _semantic=sem)
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="tla.vector"):
+        tla.simd.vreduce_max([vec, vec, tensor], _semantic=sem)

+@tr.jit
+def _vector_control_flow(out, n):
+    with tla.scope.simd():
+        acc = tla.simd.vfull(0.0, tl.float32, 64)
+        step = tla.simd.vfull(1.0, tl.float32, 64)
+        for i in range(n):
+            acc, mask = tla.simd.vadd(acc, step), tla.simd.vcmp(acc, step, "ge")
+            acc = tla.simd.vsel(mask, acc, step)
+        pair = (acc, step)
+        for i in range(n):
+            pair = (tla.simd.vadd(pair[0], pair[1]), pair[1])
+        acc = pair[0]
+        j = 0
+        while j < n:
+            acc = tla.simd.vadd(acc, step)
+            j += 1
+        if n > 0:
+            acc = tla.simd.vmul(acc, step)
+        else:
+            acc = tla.simd.vneg(acc)
+        narrow = tla.simd.vtruncf(acc, tl.bfloat16)
+        acc = tla.simd.vextf(narrow, tl.float32)
+        bits = tla.simd.vbitcast(acc, "bf16")
+        acc = tla.simd.vbitcast(bits, "f32")
+        lo, hi = tla.simd.vintlv(acc, step)
+        lo, hi = tla.simd.vdintlv(lo, hi)
+        acc = tla.simd.vreduce_max([lo, hi])
+        tla.simd.vsts(out[0], acc)
+
+
+def test_ir(output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(_vector_control_flow, {"out": tla.buffer_type((64, ), tl.float32, "ub"), "n": "i32"},

+    assert "tensor<" not in text

[ascend](feat) add A6 target support and fix option accessors (#2748)

* [ascend](feat) add A6 target support via centralized arch table

Introduce third_party/ascend/backend/ascend_arch.py as the single source of
truth for target generation, UB / RF capacity, and backend feature flags.
A6 (Ascend960 series) reuses the A5 register-based pipeline, so it is
described as a sibling generation (GEN6) instead of being hardcoded inline
at every call site.

All backend call sites that previously open-coded arch prefix checks now
delegate to the table: compiler option normalization, dtype guards, the
autotuner / ubtuner runtime helpers, and the CANN extension + libdevice
paths.  ub_size_in_kbytes_for_arch, is_ffts_supported and force_disable_ffts
delegate as well, so per-generation capacities and the FFTS policy live in
exactly one place.

Co-authored-by: yezifa <yezifa1@huawei.com>

* [compiler](fix) restore SOC detection cache and fix option accessor

Two defects surfaced once arch classification was centralized:

- utils.py: is_compile_on_910_95() declares _is_compile_on_910_95 as
  ``global`` and reads it before assigning, so the module-level binding must
  exist and be documented.  Without it the accessor raises NameError when
  called without an explicit arch, which broke test collection and the JIT
  examples that rely on runtime SOC detection.
- compiler.py: NPUOptions.compile_on_register_based was decorated with
  @property at module scope, so reading it returned the property object
  instead of a boolean and raised AttributeError on the underlying attribute.
  Provide a real accessor and bind the property to it.

Add the offline contract test covering the legacy FFTS policy, the option
accessor, the SOC cache binding, and runtime SOC detection.

* [compiler](fix) correct A6 UB capacity to 320 KB

The A6 register-based target was carrying a 376 KB unified buffer, which
overstates the real capacity.  Lower it to 320 KB in the centralized
ascend_arch generation table and align both offline contract tests.

graph_ub_budget_bytes_for_arch keeps its 80 percent cap, so the derived
graph-optimization budget moves from 308019 to 262144 bytes automatically.

* [style](NFC) reformat A6 arch table files with yapf

Run yapf (repo style: pep8 base, 120-column limit) over the centralized arch
table and its offline test so the pre-commit hook is satisfied.  Purely
mechanical: joins wrapped tuples that now fit in 120 columns and drops
manual dict-value alignment.

* [compiler](refactor) fold A6 arch classification into utils.py

Merge the centralized arch-classification table from the standalone
third_party/ascend/backend/ascend_arch.py module into utils.py, as
reviewers requested ("maybe put this into utils.py better, dont add new
files").  This collapses a new module down to one source of truth that
backends, runtime and language layers already import.

  - AscendArchGen, _ARCH_TABLE, arch_generation, is_register_based_arch,
    rf_size_in_kbytes_for_arch, ub_size_in_kbytes_for_arch and
    is_ffts_supported all move into utils.py.
  - All call sites (compiler.py, dtype_guard.py, runtime/autotuner.py,
    runtime/utils.py, runtime/cv_autotune/hardware_consts.py and the five
    cann/language extension modules) import the helpers from utils instead.
  - Remove the redundant is_ffts_disabled_arch helper: is_ffts_supported and
    force_disable_ffts already cover the two distinct policies (FTS
    capability vs. the register-based force-disable rule), so callers only
    need one FFTS predicate.
  - utils.is_register_based_arch is the public entry point;
    utils.is_compile_on_910_95 is kept as a deprecated alias that emits a
    FutureWarning pointing at is_register_based_arch, while still doing
    runtime SOC detection for callers that invoke it without an arch.

The dead self.print_autotuning assignment in the autotuner is dropped
while here: it is written but never read; the real switch is
knobs.autotuning.print.

* [compiler](fix) resolve import cycle after folding arch table into utils

Folding AscendArchGen/_ARCH_TABLE into utils.py introduced a cycle:
compiler.py imported is_register_based_arch from utils at module scope,
while utils is loaded during backend registration which in turn imports
compiler — so the symbol was not yet bound when the test ast-loader exec'd
the function body (ImportError on A3).

Fix: in compiler.py import is_register_based_arch lazily (inside
_is_register_based_target_arch, _full_row_copy_compile_options and the
NPUOptions accessor) so the helper resolves after utils finishes
initializing.  Update the offline contract test to inject a lightweight
triton.backends.ascend.utils shim, keeping it importable without an
installed Triton wheel.

No change to runtime behavior or arch policy; this only fixes the
import ordering that surfaced the cycle.

* [compiler](fix) restore original FFTS capability predicate

Folding the arch table into utils.py made is_ffts_supported drift from its
pre-refactor behaviour: the ffts_unsupported column was matched by prefix,
and unknown targets failed closed.

Ascend910A / Ascend310B4 lack FFTS support yet must not be force-disabled,
so the predicate needs two properties the table cannot express:

* the legacy names are compared exactly, not by prefix, so a distinct SOC
  such as "Ascend910A2" keeps FFTS;
* targets absent from the table default to supported, so a SOC that is not
  classified yet does not silently lose the launch-time FFTS flag.

Drop the redundant ffts_unsupported column, merge the two identical LEGACY
rows, and restore the original body on top of is_register_based_arch.
force_disable_ffts is untouched.

+"""Offline tests for the centralized Ascend arch classification table.
+
+The table lives in ``backend/utils.py``; that module pulls in pybind11 and
+triton internals, so this test execs just the classification block with
+``ast`` instead of importing it.  Runnable without an installed Triton wheel
+or an NPU runtime.
+"""
+import ast
+import unittest
+from enum import IntEnum, auto
+from pathlib import Path
+
+BACKEND = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "backend"
+
+_ARCH_FUNCTIONS = {
+    "_match_arch_entry",
+    "arch_generation",
+    "is_register_based_arch",
+    "ub_size_in_kbytes_for_arch",
+    "rf_size_in_kbytes_for_arch",
+    "is_ffts_supported",
+}
+
+# Module-level constants the extracted functions close over.
+_ARCH_CONSTANTS = {"_ARCH_TABLE", "_FFTS_UNSUPPORTED_ARCHS"}
+
+
+def load_arch_table():
+    """Extract the arch-classification block from ``utils.py``."""
+    path = BACKEND / "utils.py"
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    nodes = []
+    for node in tree.body:
+        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == "AscendArchGen":
+            nodes.append(node)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(
+                isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id in _ARCH_CONSTANTS for target in node.targets):
+            nodes.append(node)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in _ARCH_FUNCTIONS:
+            nodes.append(node)
+    namespace = {"IntEnum": IntEnum, "auto": auto}
+    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), "exec"), namespace)
+    return namespace
+
+
+class AscendArchTableTest(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.mod = load_arch_table()
+
+    def test_register_based_generations(self):
+        gen5 = self.mod["AscendArchGen"].GEN5
+        gen6 = self.mod["AscendArchGen"].GEN6
+        for arch in ("Ascend910_95", "Ascend950", "Ascend910_958b", "Ascend910_96", "Ascend960", "Ascend960DT_9691"):
+            with self.subTest(arch=arch):
+                gen = self.mod["arch_generation"](arch)
+                self.assertIn(gen, (gen5, gen6))
+                self.assertTrue(self.mod["is_register_based_arch"](arch))
+
+    def test_legacy_not_register_based(self):
+        for arch in ("Ascend910A", "Ascend910B1", "Ascend910_93", "Ascend310B", "Ascend910_97", ""):
+            with self.subTest(arch=arch):
+                self.assertFalse(self.mod["is_register_based_arch"](arch))
+
+    def test_ub_and_rf_capacity(self):
+        cases = {
+            "Ascend960": (320, 128),
+            "Ascend910_96": (320, 128),
+            "Ascend950": (256, 128),
+            "Ascend910_95": (256, 128),
+            "Ascend910B1": (192, None),
+            "Ascend910A": (192, None),
+            "Ascend910_97": (0, None),

+        }
+        for arch, (ub, rf) in cases.items():
+            with self.subTest(arch=arch):
+                self.assertEqual(self.mod["ub_size_in_kbytes_for_arch"](arch), ub)
+                self.assertEqual(self.mod["rf_size_in_kbytes_for_arch"](arch), rf)

+    def test_ffts_policy(self):

+                self.assertTrue(self.mod["is_ffts_supported"](arch))
